716: /// What counts as "user code" when deciding where to snapshot and how to
717: /// step: canonical source paths of the configured project, or any file under
718: /// the project directories.
719: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
720: pub struct UserCodeClassifier {
721:     /// Canonical user source file paths.
722:     pub files: HashSet<String>,
723:     /// Basenames of user sources (fallback when fullname is unavailable).
724:     pub basenames: HashSet<String>,
725:     /// Project directories (working dir + source parents + include dirs).
726:     pub dirs: Vec<PathBuf>,
727: }
728: 
729: impl UserCodeClassifier {
730:     pub fn from_build(build: &crate::config::BuildConfig) -> Self {
731:         let mut files = HashSet::new();
732:         let mut basenames = HashSet::new();
733:         let mut dirs = Vec::new();
734:         let mut push_source = |p: &Path| {
735:             if let (Ok(canon), true) = (std::fs::canonicalize(p), p.exists()) {
736:                 files.insert(canon.display().to_string());
737:             } else {
738:                 files.insert(p.display().to_string());
739:             }
740:             if let Some(b) = p.file_name().and_then(|b| b.to_str()) {
741:                 basenames.insert(b.to_string());
742:             }
743:             if let Some(parent) = p.parent() {
744:                 if !parent.as_os_str().is_empty() {
745:                     dirs.push(parent.to_path_buf());
746:                 }
747:             }
748:         };
749:         for s in build.user_sources() {
750:             push_source(&s);
751:         }
752:         if let Some(wd) = &build.working_directory {
753:             if wd.is_dir() {
754:                 dirs.push(wd.clone());
755:             }
756:         }
757:         for d in &build.include_dirs {
758:             dirs.push(d.clone());
759:         }
760:         Self {
761:             files,
762:             basenames,
763:             dirs,
764:         }
765:     }
766: 
767:     pub fn is_user_file(&self, frame: &StackFrameInfo) -> bool {
768:         let candidates: [Option<&str>; 2] = [
769:             frame.full_file.as_deref(),
770:             frame.file.as_deref(),
771:         ];
772:         for cand in candidates.iter().flatten() {
773:             let path = Path::new(cand);
774:             if let Ok(canon) = std::fs::canonicalize(path) {
775:                 if self.files.contains(canon.display().to_string().as_str()) {
776:                     return true;
777:                 }
778:             }
779:             if self.files.contains(*cand) {
780:                 return true;
781:             }
782:             let lowered = cand.to_string();
783:             if self
784:                 .dirs
785:                 .iter()
786:                 .any(|d| lowered.starts_with(&format!("{}/", d.display())))
787:             {
788:                 return true;
789:             }
790:             if path.is_absolute() {
791:                 if let Some(base) = path.file_name().and_then(|b| b.to_str()) {
792:                     if self.basenames.contains(base) {
793:                         return true;
794:                     }
795:                 }
796:             }
797:         }
798:         false
799:     }
800: }

802: /// Options controlling per-stop data collection.
803: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
804: pub struct CaptureOptions {
805:     pub classifier: UserCodeClassifier,
806:     pub max_variables: usize,
807:     pub max_memory_read: usize,
808:     /// Per-snapshot memory budget for raw byte reads (variables only; heap
809:     /// reads are budgeted by the orchestrator on top of this).
810:     pub memory_budget: usize,
811: }
812: 
813: /// GDB-side state captured at one stop.
814: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
815: pub struct CapturedState {
816:     pub frames: Vec<StackFrameInfo>,
817:     pub current: Option<StackFrameInfo>,
818:     pub is_user_code: bool,
819:     pub variables: Vec<VariableInfo>,
820:     /// Bytes spent on variable raw-byte reads in this capture.
821:     pub memory_used: usize,
822: }
823: 
824: /// Capture frames + variables (+ per-variable raw bytes) at a stop.
825: pub async fn capture_state(
826:     session: &mut GdbSession,
827:     opts: &CaptureOptions,
828: ) -> Result<CapturedState> {
829:     let mut state = CapturedState::default();
830: 
831:     let frames_resp = session.execute("-stack-list-frames").await?;
832:     state.frames = parse_frames(&frames_resp.record);
833:     state.current = state.frames.first().cloned();
834:     state.is_user_code = state
835:         .current
836:         .as_ref()
837:         .map(|f| opts.classifier.is_user_file(f))
838:         .unwrap_or(false);
839: 
840:     if !state.is_user_code {
841:         return Ok(state);
842:     }
843: 
844:     let vars_resp = session.execute("-stack-list-variables --all-values").await?;
845:     let raw_vars = parse_variables(&vars_resp.record);
846:     let budget = &mut state.memory_used;
847: 
848:     for raw in raw_vars.iter().take(opts.max_variables) {
849:         let mut var = VariableInfo {
850:             name: raw.name.clone(),
851:             value: raw.value.clone(),
852:             is_argument: Some(raw.is_argument),
853:             ..Default::default()
854:         };
855: 
856:         // Type via console `whatis` (one command, no varobj bookkeeping).
857:         match session
858:             .execute(&format!(
859:                 "-interpreter-exec console \"whatis {}\"",
860:                 raw.name
861:             ))
862:             .await
863:         {
864:             Ok(resp) => {
865:                 var.c_type = extract_type_from_streams(&resp.streams);
866:             }
867:             Err(e) => var.read_error = Some(e.to_string()),
868:         }
869: 
870:         // Address of the variable itself.
871:         if let Ok(addr_val) = session.evaluate(&format!("&{}", raw.name)).await {
872:             var.address = extract_hex_address(&addr_val);
873:         }
874: 
875:         // Size (runtime-evaluated, works for VLAs too).
876:         if let Ok(size_val) = session.evaluate(&format!("sizeof({})", raw.name)).await {
877:             var.size_bytes = size_val.trim().parse::<u64>().ok();
878:         }
879: 
880:         // For pointer variables: the address stored INSIDE the pointer.
881:         // The pointer's own address is `var.address`; never conflated.
882:         if var.c_type.contains('*') {
883:             if let Ok(target) = session
884:                 .evaluate(&format!("(unsigned long)({})", raw.name))
885:                 .await
886:             {
887:                 if let Ok(n) = target.trim().parse::<u64>() {
888:                     var.points_to = Some(format!("0x{n:x}"));
889:                 }
890:             }
891:         }
892: 
893:         // Raw bytes of the variable itself, within budget.
894:         let mut err = var.read_error.take();
895:         if let (Some(addr), Some(size)) = (&var.address, var.size_bytes) {
896:             let read_size = size.min(opts.max_memory_read as u64);
897:             if *budget + read_size as usize <= opts.memory_budget {
898:                 match session.read_memory_bytes(addr, read_size).await {
899:                     Ok(hex) => {
900:                         *budget += read_size as usize;
901:                         var.raw_bytes_hex = Some(hex);
902:                     }
903:                     Err(e) => err = Some(format!("memory read failed: {e}")),
904:                 }
905:             } else {
906:                 err = Some("snapshot memory budget exhausted".into());
907:             }
908:         }
909:         var.read_error = err;
910:         state.variables.push(var);
911:     }
912: 
913:     Ok(state)
914: }

916: /// Pull `type = ...` out of console-command stream output (`whatis`).
917: fn extract_type_from_streams(streams: &[StreamRecord]) -> String {
918:     for (kind, text) in streams.iter().rev() {
919:         if matches!(kind, StreamKind::Console | StreamKind::Log) {
920:             for line in text.lines() {
921:                 if let Some(rest) = line.trim().strip_prefix("type = ") {
922:                     return rest.trim().to_string();
923:                 }
924:             }
925:         }
926:     }
927:     String::new()
928: }

930: /// Quote a value as a single MI c-string argument.
931: fn quote_for_mi(value: &str) -> String {
932:     let mut out = String::with_capacity(value.len() + 2);
933:     out.push('"');
934:     for c in value.chars() {
935:         match c {
936:             '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
937:             '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
938:             '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
939:             '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
940:             '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
941:             other => out.push(other),
942:         }
943:     }
944:     out.push('"');
945:     out
946: }

952: async fn reader_task(stdout: ChildStdout, shared: Arc<Shared>) {
953:     let mut reader = BufReader::new(stdout);
954:     let mut line_buf = Vec::new();
955:     loop {
956:         line_buf.clear();
957:         match reader.read_until(b'\n', &mut line_buf).await {
958:             Ok(0) => break,
959:             Ok(_) => {
960:                 let line = String::from_utf8_lossy(&line_buf);
961:                 handle_line(&line, &shared);
962:             }
963:             Err(_) => break,
964:         }
965:     }
966:     // EOF: fail every pending command.
967:     shared.eof.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
968:     let mut pending = shared.pending.lock().unwrap();
969:     for (_, tx) in pending.drain() {
970:         let _ = tx.send(Err("gdb exited".into()));
971:     }
972: }
973: 
974: fn handle_line(line: &str, shared: &Shared) {
975:     let trimmed = line.trim_end_matches(['\n', '\r']);
976:     if trimmed.is_empty() || trimmed.starts_with("(gdb)") {
977:         return;
978:     }
979:     if shared.debug_echo {
980:         let mut console = shared.console.lock().unwrap();
981:         if console.len() < MAX_CONSOLE_LOG_BYTES {
982:             console.push_str("[raw] ");
983:             console.push_str(trimmed);
984:             console.push('\n');
985:         }
986:     }
987:     match parse_line(trimmed) {
988:         Ok(Some(record)) => route_record(record, shared),
989:         Ok(None) => {}
990:         Err(e) => {
991:             let mut console = shared.console.lock().unwrap();
992:             if console.len() < MAX_CONSOLE_LOG_BYTES {
993:                 console.push_str("[unparsed] ");
994:                 console.push_str(trimmed);
995:                 console.push_str(" (");
996:                 console.push_str(&e.to_string());
997:                 console.push_str(")\n");
998:             }
999:         }
1000:     }
1001: }
1002: 
1003: fn route_record(record: MiRecord, shared: &Shared) {
1004:     match &record {
1005:         MiRecord::Stream { kind, text } => {
1006:             match kind {
1007:                 StreamKind::Console | StreamKind::Log => {
1008:                     let mut console = shared.console.lock().unwrap();
1009:                     if console.len() < MAX_CONSOLE_LOG_BYTES {
1010:                         console.push_str(text);
1011:                     }
1012:                 }
1013:                 StreamKind::Target => {
1014:                     // Target stream (`@`) only appears when the inferior is
1015:                     // NOT attached to a pty; treat as program output.
1016:                     let mut program = shared.program.lock().unwrap();
1017:                     program.push(text.as_bytes(), shared.output_cap);
1018:                 }
1019:             }
1020:             // Collect for the in-flight command (console commands such as
1021:             // `whatis` deliver their result through stream records).
1022:             shared.current_streams.lock().unwrap().push((*kind, text.clone()));
1023:         }
1024:         MiRecord::Result { token, .. } | MiRecord::Exec { token, .. } => {
1025:             if let Some(tok) = token {
1026:                 let sender = shared.pending.lock().unwrap().remove(tok);
1027:                 if let Some(tx) = sender {
1028:                     let streams = {
1029:                         let mut guard = shared.current_streams.lock().unwrap();
1030:                         std::mem::take(&mut *guard)
1031:                     };
1032:                     let _ = tx.send(Ok((record, streams)));
1033:                     return;
1034:                 }
1035:             }
1036:             // Async record (*running / *stopped / unexpected result).
1037:             let _ = shared.async_tx.send(record);
1038:         }
1039:         MiRecord::Notify { .. } => {
1040:             let _ = shared.async_tx.send(record);
1041:         }
1042:     }
1043: }

1045: async fn pty_reader_task(master: OwnedFd, shared: Arc<Shared>) {
1046:     use tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd;
1047:     let fd = match unsafe { AsyncFd::register(master) } {
1048:         Ok(fd) => fd,
1049:         Err(_) => return,
1050:     };
1051:     loop {
1052:         let mut guard = match fd.readable().await {
1053:             Ok(g) => g,
1054:             Err(_) => break,
1055:         };
1056:         let mut buf = [0u8; 4096];
1057:         let result = guard.try_io(|inner| {
1058:             let fd = inner.get_ref().as_raw_fd();
1059:             let n = unsafe {
1060:                 libc::read(
1061:                     fd,
1062:                     buf.as_mut_ptr() as *mut libc::c_void,
1063:                     buf.len(),
1064:                 )
1065:             };
1066:             if n < 0 {
1067:                 // EAGAIN => try again later; EIO => slave closed.
1068:                 return Err(std::io::Error::last_os_error());
1069:             }
1070:             std::io::Result::Ok(n as usize)
1071:         });
1072:         match result {
1073:             Ok(Ok(0)) => break,          // closed
1074:             Ok(Ok(n)) => {
1075:                 let mut program = shared.program.lock().unwrap();
1076:                 program.push(&buf[..n], shared.output_cap);
1077:             }
1078:             Ok(Err(e)) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => continue,
1079:             // EIO on Linux: all slave sides closed (inferior exited).
1080:             Ok(Err(_)) => break,
1081:             Err(_) => continue,
1082:         }
1083:     }
1084: }

3: //! The engine compiles the project twice: a **debug binary** (with the

13: //! format into [`CompilerDiagnostic`]. Linker errors (not covered by either

99: pub async fn probe_tool(tool: &str, version_arg: &str) -> Result<String> {

105:         .output()
106:         .await

112:         return Err(EngineError::MissingTool {
113:             tool: tool_owned.clone(),
114:             reason: format!("`{} {}` failed", tool_owned, version_display),

118:     Ok(text.lines().next().unwrap_or_default().to_string())

121: /// Probe which diagnostics format the compiler supports. GCC 16 removed
122: /// `json`; GCC ≥ 15 offers SARIF; older versions offer JSON.
123: pub async fn detect_diagnostics_format(cc: &str) -> DiagnosticsFormat {
124:     for (fmt, flag) in [
125:         (DiagnosticsFormat::LegacyJson, "-fdiagnostics-format=json"),
126:         (
127:             DiagnosticsFormat::Sarif,
128:             "-fdiagnostics-format=sarif-stderr",
129:         ),
130:     ] {
131:         let probe = Command::new(cc)
132:             .args(["-x", "c", "-fsyntax-only", flag, "/dev/null"])
133:             .output()
134:             .await;
135:         match probe {
136:             Ok(out) => {
137:                 let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr);
138:                 if stderr.contains("unrecognized argument in option") {
139:                     continue; // flag unsupported, try next
140:                 }
141:                 return fmt;
142:             }
143:             Err(_) => continue,
144:         }
145:     }
146:     DiagnosticsFormat::Text
147: }

1: //! Independent Valgrind memcheck execution and XML report parsing.
2: //!
3: //! Valgrind runs in its own subprocess with `--xml-file` capturing the
4: //! machine-readable report away from both the program's stdout (captured
5: //! separately) and its stderr (captured separately). The XML is parsed with
6: //! `roxmltree` — a real XML parser, never regex.
7: //!
8: //! The documented command template in the spec used `--xml-fd=2`; the engine
9: //! deliberately uses `--xml-file` instead: with `--xml-fd=2` the client's
10: //! stderr writes land on the same descriptor as the XML stream and can
11: //! corrupt it mid-document. `--xml-file` keeps XML, program stdout and
12: //! program stderr on three separate channels (see README "Deviations").
13: //!
14: //! Valgrind reports allocation *summaries* and memory *errors* with source
15: //! locations. It does not report a time-indexed heap history — that is the
16: //! job of the allocation instrumentation + GDB memory reads.

167: /// Parse a Valgrind memcheck XML document.
168: pub fn parse_valgrind_xml(xml: &str) -> Result<ValgrindReport> {
169:     let doc = roxmltree::Document::parse(xml)
170:         .map_err(|e| EngineError::Valgrind(format!("XML parse error: {e}")))?;
171:     let root = doc.root_element();
172:     if root.tag_name().name() != "valgrindoutput" {
173:         return Err(EngineError::Valgrind(
174:             "unexpected XML root (expected valgrindoutput)".into(),
175:         ));
176:     }
177: 
178:     let mut report = ValgrindReport::default();
179: 
180:     for child in root.children() {
181:         if !child.is_element() {
182:             continue;
183:         }
184:         match child.tag_name().name() {
185:             "heap_summary" => {
186:                 if let Some(in_use) = child.children().find(|c| c.tag_name().name() == "memory_in_use_at_exit") {
187:                     report.bytes_in_use_at_exit = child_text_u64(in_use, "bytes");
188:                     report.blocks_in_use_at_exit = child_text_u64(in_use, "blocks");
189:                 }
190:                 if let Some(total) = child.children().find(|c| c.tag_name().name() == "total_heap_usage") {
191:                     report.total_allocs = child_text_u64(total, "allocs");
192:                     report.total_frees = child_text_u64(total, "frees");
193:                     report.bytes_allocated = child_text_u64(total, "bytes_allocated");
194:                 }
195:             }
196:             "all_heap_blocks_freed" => {
197:                 report.all_heap_blocks_freed = child.text().map(|t| t.trim() == "true");
198:             }
199:             "error" => {
200:                 let err = parse_error(child);
201:                 // Leak classification by kind.
202:                 match err.kind.as_str() {
203:                     "Leak_DefinitelyLost" => report.definitely_lost_bytes += err.leaked_bytes,
204:                     "Leak_IndirectlyLost" => report.indirectly_lost_bytes += err.leaked_bytes,
205:                     "Leak_PossiblyLost" => report.possibly_lost_bytes += err.leaked_bytes,
206:                     "Leak_StillReachable" => report.still_reachable_bytes += err.leaked_bytes,
207:                     _ => {}
208:                 }
209:                 // Human-readable summary string with the first user site.
210:                 let site = err
211:                     .stack
212:                     .iter()
213:                     .find(|f| f.file.is_some())
214:                     .map(|f| format!("{}:{}", f.file.clone().unwrap_or_default(), f.line.unwrap_or(0)))
215:                     .unwrap_or_default();
216:                 report.errors.push(if site.is_empty() {
217:                     format!("{}: {}", err.kind, err.what)
218:                 } else {
219:                     format!("{}: {} ({})", err.kind, err.what, site)
220:                 });
221:                 report.detailed_errors.push(err);
222:             }
223:             _ => {}
224:         }
225:     }
226:     Ok(report)
227: }
228: 
229: fn child_text_u64(node: roxmltree::Node, tag: &str) -> u64 {
230:     node.children()
231:         .find(|c| c.tag_name().name() == tag)
232:         .and_then(|c| c.text())
233:         .and_then(|t| t.trim().parse().ok())
234:         .unwrap_or(0)
235: }

951: fn char_safe_head(s: &str, cap_bytes: usize) -> String {
952:     if s.len() <= cap_bytes {
953:         return s.to_string();
954:     }
955:     let mut cut = cap_bytes;
956:     while !s.is_char_boundary(cut) {
957:         cut -= 1;
958:     }
959:     s[..cut].to_string()
960: }

962: fn crash_from(stop: &StoppedInfo, state: &crate::gdb_mi::CapturedState) -> CrashReport {
963:     let frame = stop.frame.clone().or_else(|| state.current.clone());
964:     CrashReport {
965:         signal_name: stop
966:             .signal_name
967:             .clone()
968:             .unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".into()),
969:         file: frame.as_ref().and_then(|f| f.file.clone()),
970:         line: frame.as_ref().and_then(|f| f.line),
971:         func: frame
972:             .as_ref()
973:             .map(|f| f.func.clone())
974:             .filter(|s| !s.is_empty()),
975:         asan_summary: None,
976:         backtrace: state.frames.clone(),
977:         detail: stop.signal_meaning.clone(),

981: /// Inferior exit code: from the stop record, else from the
982: /// `=thread-group-exited` notification in the backlog. MI emits the value as
983: /// decimal in current versions but hex in some older ones; both accepted.
984: fn exit_code_from(session: &mut GdbSession, stop: &StoppedInfo) -> Option<i32> {
985:     if let Some(code) = &stop.exit_code {
986:         return parse_mi_exit_code(code);
987:     }
988:     for record in session.take_backlog() {
989:         if let crate::mi_parser::MiRecord::Notify { class, results } = &record {
990:             if class == "thread-group-exited" {
991:                 for r in results {
992:                     if r.variable == "exit-code" {
993:                         if let Some(v) = crate::mi_parser::as_const(&r.value) {
994:                             if let Some(c) = parse_mi_exit_code(v) {
995:                                 return Some(c);
996:                             }
997:                         }
998:                     }
999:                 }
1000:             }
1001:         }
1002:     }
1003:     None
1004: }
1005: 
1006: fn parse_mi_exit_code(text: &str) -> Option<i32> {
1007:     if let Ok(v) = text.parse::<i32>() {
1008:         return Some(v);
1009:     }
1010:     u32::from_str_radix(text, 16).ok().map(|v| v as i32)
1011: }

1017: fn infer_parent_pid(timeline: &HeapTimeline, inferior_pid: Option<u32>) -> Option<u32> {
1018:     if let Some(pid) = inferior_pid {
1019:         return Some(pid);
1020:     }
1021:     let pids = timeline.pids_seen();
1022:     if pids.len() == 1 {
1023:         Some(pids[0])
1024:     } else {
1025:         None
1026:     }
1027: }

1029: /// Fill snapshot heap blocks with resolved allocation locations and global
1030: /// (pid-widened) ids.
1031: fn backfill_snapshots(
1032:     timeline: &HeapTimeline,
1033:     mut snapshots: Vec<ExecutionSnapshot>,
1034:     parent_pid: Option<u32>,
1035: ) -> Vec<ExecutionSnapshot> {
1036:     let Some(parent_pid) = parent_pid else {
1037:         return snapshots;
1038:     };
1039:     for snap in snapshots.iter_mut() {
1040:         for block in snap.heap_blocks.iter_mut() {
1041:             if let Some(state) = timeline.block_by_id(parent_pid, block.allocation_id) {
1042:                 block.allocation_file = state.caller_file.clone();
1043:                 block.allocation_line = state.caller_line;
1044:                 block.realloc_from_id = state
1045:                     .realloc_from_id
1046:                     .map(|id| timeline.global_id(parent_pid, id));
1047:                 block.allocation_id = timeline.global_id(parent_pid, block.allocation_id);
1048:             }
1049:         }
1050:     }
1051:     snapshots
1052: }
1053: 
1054: /// Serialized heap events with pid-widened ids when multiple processes ran.
1055: fn final_events(timeline: &HeapTimeline) -> Vec<crate::models::HeapEvent> {
1056:     timeline
1057:         .events()
1058:         .iter()
1059:         .map(|e| {
1060:             let mut e = e.clone();
1061:             e.allocation_id = timeline.global_id(e.pid, e.allocation_id);
1062:             if let Some(old) = e.old_allocation_id {
1063:                 e.old_allocation_id = Some(timeline.global_id(e.pid, old));
1064:             }
1065:             e
1066:         })
1067:         .collect()
1068: }
1069: 
1070: /// Final heap state: every reconstructed block with its end-of-run status.
1071: /// `raw_bytes_hex` carries the last bytes captured while the block was alive
1072: /// (from any snapshot); freed blocks keep that historical capture, live
1073: /// blocks the most recent one.
1074: fn build_heap_state(
1075:     timeline: &HeapTimeline,
1076:     snapshots: &[ExecutionSnapshot],
1077:     parent_pid: Option<u32>,
1078: ) -> Vec<HeapBlockInfo> {
1079:     let mut last_contents: HashMap<u64, String> = HashMap::new();
1080:     for snap in snapshots {
1081:         for b in &snap.heap_blocks {
1082:             if let Some(hex) = &b.raw_bytes_hex {
1083:                 last_contents.insert(b.allocation_id, hex.clone());
1084:             }
1085:         }
1086:     }
1087:     timeline
1088:         .blocks()
1089:         .iter()
1090:         .map(|b| {
1091:             let global = parent_pid
1092:                 .map(|p| timeline.global_id(p, b.allocation_id))
1093:                 .unwrap_or(b.allocation_id);
1094:             HeapBlockInfo {
1095:                 allocation_id: global,
1096:                 address: format!("0x{:x}", b.addr),
1097:                 size_bytes: b.size,
1098:                 allocation_type: b.alloc_type.to_string(),
1099:                 is_freed: b.freed,
1100:                 allocation_file: b.caller_file.clone(),
1101:                 allocation_line: b.caller_line,
1102:                 raw_bytes_hex: last_contents.get(&global).cloned(),
1103:                 memory_read_error: None,
1104:                 realloc_from_id: b.realloc_from_id.map(|id| timeline.global_id(b.pid, id)),
1105:             }
1106:         })
1107:         .collect()
1108: }

1110: fn make_session_dir() -> Result<PathBuf> {
1111:     let nanos = SystemTime::now()
1112:         .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
1113:         .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
1114:         .unwrap_or(0);
1115:     let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("c-trace-{}-{}", std::process::id(), nanos));
1116:     std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir)?;
1117:     Ok(dir)
1118: }

358: /// Build the full gcc argument vector for one binary.
359: fn build_argv(
360:     build: &BuildConfig,
361:     opts: &CompileOptions,
362:     diag_flag: Option<&str>,
363: ) -> Vec<String> {
364:     let mut argv: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
365: 
366:     // --- engine-required flags (kept separate from user flags) ---
367:     argv.push("-g".into());
368:     argv.push("-O0".into());
369:     argv.push("-fno-omit-frame-pointer".into());
370:     if opts.sanitized {
371:         argv.push(format!("-fsanitize={}", opts.sanitizer_variant));
372:     }
373:     if let Some(flag) = diag_flag {
374:         argv.push(flag.into());
375:     }
376:     if opts.include_alloc_tracker {
377:         argv.extend(
378:             [
379:                 "-Wl,--wrap=malloc",
380:                 "-Wl,--wrap=calloc",
381:                 "-Wl,--wrap=realloc",
382:                 "-Wl,--wrap=free",
383:             ]
384:             .iter()
385:             .map(|s| s.to_string()),
386:         );
387:     }
388: 
389:     // --- user configuration ---
390:     for d in &build.defines {
391:         argv.push(format!("-D{}", d));
392:     }
393:     for dir in &build.include_dirs {
394:         argv.push(format!("-I{}", dir.display()));
395:     }
396:     argv.extend(build.compiler_flags.iter().cloned());
397: 
398:     // --- inputs ---
399:     argv.push(build.source_file.display().to_string());
400:     for s in &build.additional_sources {
401:         argv.push(s.display().to_string());
402:     }
403:     if let Some(tracker) = &opts.tracker_source {
404:         argv.push(tracker.display().to_string());
405:     }
406:     for o in &build.object_files {
407:         argv.push(o.display().to_string());
408:     }
409: 
410:     // --- linking ---
411:     for dir in &build.library_dirs {
412:         argv.push(format!("-L{}", dir.display()));
413:     }
414:     argv.extend(build.linker_flags.iter().cloned());
415:     for lib in &build.libraries {
416:         argv.push(format!("-l{}", lib));
417:     }
418: 
419:     argv.push("-o".into());
420:     argv.push(opts.output_path.display().to_string());
421:     argv
422: }

424: /// Compile (and link) the configured project once.
425: pub async fn compile(
426:     build: &BuildConfig,
427:     cc: &str,
428:     opts: &CompileOptions,
429:     format: DiagnosticsFormat,
430: ) -> Result<CompilationOutput> {
431:     if build.source_file.as_os_str().is_empty() {
432:         return Err(EngineError::Config("no source file configured".into()));
433:     }
434:     let diag_flag = match format {
435:         DiagnosticsFormat::LegacyJson => Some("-fdiagnostics-format=json"),
436:         DiagnosticsFormat::Sarif => Some("-fdiagnostics-format=sarif-stderr"),
437:         DiagnosticsFormat::Text => None,
438:     };
439:     let argv = build_argv(build, opts, diag_flag);
440: 
441:     let mut cmd = Command::new(cc);
442:     cmd.args(&argv);
443:     if let Some(dir) = &build.working_directory {
444:         cmd.current_dir(dir);
445:     }
446:     // Compilation gets its own generous ceiling; the execution limits apply
447:     // to the inferior, not to the compiler.
448:     let output = tokio::time::timeout(
449:         std::time::Duration::from_secs(300),
450:         cmd.output(),
451:     )
452:     .await
453:     .map_err(|_| EngineError::Other("compilation timed out after 300s".into()))?
454:     .map_err(EngineError::Io)?;
455: 
456:     let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).into_owned();
457:     let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).into_owned();
458:     let _ = stdout; // gcc diagnostics go to stderr
459: 
460:     let success = output.status.success();
461: 
462:     let diagnostics = match format {
463:         DiagnosticsFormat::LegacyJson => {
464:             parse_legacy_gcc_json(&stderr).unwrap_or_else(|| text_diagnostics(&stderr))
465:         }
466:         DiagnosticsFormat::Sarif => {
467:             parse_sarif(&stderr).unwrap_or_else(|| text_diagnostics(&stderr))
468:         }
469:         DiagnosticsFormat::Text => {
470:             // Text mode: only produce a diagnostic when the build failed or
471:             // stderr is non-empty (warnings are unparseable in text mode but
472:             // must not be lost).
473:             if success && stderr.trim().is_empty() {
474:                 Vec::new()
475:             } else {
476:                 text_diagnostics(&stderr)
477:             }
478:         }
479:     };
480:     // In JSON modes gcc prints only the diagnostic JSON; if the toolchain
481:     // succeeded but no diagnostics came back, that is normal (no warnings).
482:     let has_errors = diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.kind == "error" || d.kind == "linker-error" || d.kind == "fatal error");
483:     let success = success && !has_errors;
484: 
485:     Ok(CompilationOutput {
486:         success,
487:         exit_code: output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1),
488:         binary_path: opts.output_path.clone(),
489:         diagnostics,
490:         raw_stderr: stderr,
491:         diagnostics_format: format,
492:     })
493: }
494: 
495: /// Convenience: compile with the standard engine layout for one session dir.
496: pub async fn compile_project(
497:     build: &BuildConfig,
498:     session_dir: &Path,
499:     tracker_source: Option<PathBuf>,
500: ) -> Result<(CompilationOutput, CompilationOutput)> {
501:     let cc = "gcc";
502:     let _gcc_version = probe_tool(cc, "--version").await?;
503:     let format = detect_diagnostics_format(cc).await;
504: 
505:     let debug_name = build
506:         .output_name
507:         .clone()
508:         .unwrap_or_else(|| "program".to_string());
509:     let debug_out = session_dir.join(format!("{}_debug", debug_name));
510: 
511:     let debug_opts = CompileOptions::debug(debug_out, tracker_source);
512:     let debug_result = compile(build, cc, &debug_opts, format).await?;
513: 
514:     if !debug_result.success {
515:         return Ok((debug_result, not_built()));
516:     }
517: 
518:     // The sanitized build reuses the user's configuration but not the
519:     // instrumentation runtime: ASan replaces the allocator at interception
520:     // level, and wrapping the allocator underneath ASan would double-report.
521:     // Sanitizer runtimes may be partially installed (e.g. libasan present but
522:     // libubsan missing), so degrade: combined → asan-only → ubsan-only → none.
523:     let asan_out = session_dir.join(format!("{}_asan", debug_name));
524:     let variants: [(&'static str, &'static str); 3] = [
525:         ("address,undefined", "asan+ubsan"),
526:         ("address", "asan"),
527:         ("undefined", "ubsan"),
528:     ];
529:     let mut asan_result = not_built();
530:     for (flag, _label) in variants {
531:         let opts = CompileOptions::sanitized_with_variant(asan_out.clone(), flag);
532:         let r = compile(build, cc, &opts, format).await?;
533:         if r.success {
534:             asan_result = r;
535:             break;
536:         }
537:     }
538: 
539:     Ok((debug_result, asan_result))
540: }

547:         diagnostics: Vec::new(),
548:         raw_stderr: String::new(),

19: #[tokio::main]
20: async fn main() -> ExitCode {
21:     let cli = Cli::parse();
22: 
23:     let config = match cli.to_config() {
24:         Ok(config) => config,
25:         Err(e) => {
26:             eprintln!("error: {e}");
27:             return ExitCode::from(1);
28:         }
29:     };
30:

33:             let json = if config.pretty {
34:                 serde_json::to_string_pretty(&trace)
35:             } else {
36:                 serde_json::to_string(&trace)
37:             };
38:             match json {
39:                 Ok(json) => {
40:                     if let Some(out) = &config.output_file {
41:                         if let Err(e) = std::fs::write(out, format!("{json}\n")) {
42:                             eprintln!("error: cannot write output file {}: {e}", out.display());
43:                             return ExitCode::from(1);
44:                         }
45:                     }
46:                     // Trace to stdout. When a file was requested too, the
47:                     // stdout stream is the same JSON document.
48:                     let mut stdout = std::io::stdout().lock();
49:                     let _ = writeln!(stdout, "{json}");
50:                     let _ = stdout.flush();
51: 
52:                     if !trace.compiled_successfully {
53:                         return ExitCode::from(2);
54:                     }
55:                     ExitCode::SUCCESS
56:                 }
57:                 Err(e) => {
58:                     eprintln!("error: cannot serialize trace: {e}");
59:                     ExitCode::from(1)
60:                 }
61:             }
62:         }
63:         Err(e) => {
64:             eprintln!("error: {e}");
65:             ExitCode::from(1)
66:         }
67:     }
68: }

16: /// Command line interface.
17: ///
18: /// Program arguments come after `--` (e.g. `cargo run -- sample.c -- 1 2 3`)
19: /// or via repeated `--arg` flags; they are handed to the traced program and
20: /// never to the compiler.

139: impl Cli {
140:     /// Build the effective [`TraceConfig`] with precedence
141:     /// CLI > JSON config file > defaults.
142:     pub fn to_config(&self) -> Result<TraceConfig> {
143:         // 1. JSON config file (optional).
144:         let file: ConfigFile = match &self.config {
145:             Some(path) => {
146:                 let text = std::fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| EngineError::Config(format!(
147:                     "cannot read config file {}: {e}",
148:                     path.display()
149:                 )))?;
150:                 serde_json::from_str(&text).map_err(|e| {
151:                     EngineError::Config(format!("invalid config file {}: {e}", path.display()))
152:                 })?
153:             }
154:             None => ConfigFile::default(),
155:         };
156: 
157:         // 2. Source resolution: --source > positional > config file.
158:         let source = self
159:             .source
160:             .clone()
161:             .or_else(|| self.source_positional.clone())
162:             .or_else(|| file.source.clone())
163:             .ok_or_else(|| {
164:                 EngineError::Config(
165:                     "no source file given (pass a .c file or --source <file>)".into(),
166:                 )
167:             })?;
168:         if !source.is_file() {
169:             return Err(EngineError::Config(format!(
170:                 "source file not found: {}",
171:                 source.display()
172:             )));
173:         }
174: 
175:         let mut build = file_build(&file, &source);
176:         // CLI list flags APPEND to the config file's lists.
177:         build.additional_sources.extend(self.add_source.iter().cloned());
178:         build.include_dirs.extend(self.include_dir.iter().cloned());
179:         build.defines.extend(self.define.iter().cloned());
180:         build.compiler_flags.extend(self.compiler_flag.iter().cloned());
181:         build.linker_flags.extend(self.linker_flag.iter().cloned());
182:         build.library_dirs.extend(self.library_dir.iter().cloned());
183:         build.libraries.extend(self.library.iter().cloned());
184:         build.object_files.extend(self.object_file.iter().cloned());
185:         if self.output_name.is_some() {
186:             build.output_name = self.output_name.clone();
187:         }
188:         if self.working_directory.is_some() {
189:             build.working_directory = self.working_directory.clone();
190:         }
191: 
192:         // 3. Program arguments: config file + --arg flags + trailing args.
193:         let mut program_args = file.program_args.clone();
194:         program_args.extend(self.arg.iter().cloned());
195:         program_args.extend(self.program_args.iter().cloned());
196: 
197:         let mut limits = file.limits.clone().unwrap_or_default();
198:         if let Some(v) = self.max_steps {
199:             limits.max_steps = v;
200:         }
201:         if let Some(v) = self.timeout {
202:             limits.timeout_seconds = v;
203:         }
204:         if let Some(v) = self.max_memory_mb {
205:             limits.max_memory_mb = v;
206:         }
207:         if let Some(v) = self.max_output_bytes {
208:             limits.max_output_bytes = v;
209:         }
210:         if let Some(v) = self.max_heap_allocations {
211:             limits.max_heap_allocations = v;
212:         }
213:         if let Some(v) = self.max_snapshots {
214:             limits.max_snapshot_count = v;
215:         }
216:         if let Some(v) = self.max_snapshot_memory_bytes {
217:             limits.max_snapshot_memory_bytes = v;
218:         }
219:         if let Some(v) = self.max_memory_read_bytes {
220:             limits.max_memory_read_bytes = v;
221:         }
222:         if let Some(v) = self.max_processes {
223:             limits.max_process_count = v;
224:         }
225:         if let Some(v) = self.max_variables {
226:             limits.max_variables_per_snapshot = v;
227:         }
228: 
229:         let pretty = if self.no_pretty {
230:             false
231:         } else {
232:             file.pretty.unwrap_or(true)
233:         };
234:         let keep_temp = self.keep_temp || file.keep_temp.unwrap_or(false);
235:         let output_file = self.output.clone().or(file.output_file.clone());
236: 
237:         Ok(TraceConfig {
238:             build,
239:             program_args,
240:             inferior_working_directory: self
241:                 .inferior_working_directory
242:                 .clone()
243:                 .or(file.inferior_working_directory.clone()),
244:             limits,
245:             output_file,
246:             pretty,
247:             keep_temp,
248:         })
249:     }
250: }

1: //! # c-trace-engine
2: //!
3: //! Standalone Rust backend that compiles a configurable C project with GCC,
4: //! executes it under GDB (Machine Interface 2), records execution snapshots
5: //! and heap allocation events, performs an independent Valgrind analysis, and
6: //! emits one structured, serializable [`models::DebugSessionTrace`].
7: //!
8: //! Module map (see README for the full architecture):
9: //!
10: //! | Module                | Responsibility                                        |
11: //! |-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|
12: //! | `models`              | Serializable trace data model                          |
13: //! | `config`              | `BuildConfig`, `TraceConfig`, JSON config files        |
14: //! | `resource_limits`     | `ExecutionLimits` + rlimit/cgroup enforcement          |
15: //! | `compiler`            | GCC invocation + JSON/SARIF diagnostic parsing         |
16: //! | `mi_parser`           | GDB MI2 tokenizer + recursive-descent parser (`nom`)   |
17: //! | `gdb_mi`              | Async GDB session: pty, tokens, stepping, snapshots    |
18: //! | `allocation_tracker`  | C instrumentation runtime + event ingestion            |
19: //! | `valgrind`            | Independent Valgrind run + XML parsing                 |
20: //! | `sanitizer`           | Separate ASan/UBSan diagnostic pass                    |
21: //! | `trace`               | Orchestrates the complete pipeline                     |
22: //! | `cli`                 | Argument parsing and config merging                    |
23:

148: /// Incremental reader for the event trace file.
149: pub struct EventFileReader {
150:     path: PathBuf,
151:     offset: u64,
152:     partial: Vec<u8>,
153:     pub parse_errors: Vec<String>,
154: }
155: 
156: impl EventFileReader {
157:     pub fn new(path: PathBuf) -> Self {
158:         Self {
159:             path,
160:             offset: 0,
161:             partial: Vec::new(),
162:             parse_errors: Vec::new(),
163:         }
164:     }
165: 
166:     /// Read and parse all events appended since the last call. Partial
167:     /// trailing lines (crash mid-write) are buffered until complete.
168:     pub fn read_new(&mut self) -> Vec<RawEvent> {
169:         let mut events = Vec::new();
170:         let file = match File::open(&self.path) {
171:             Ok(f) => f,
172:             Err(_) => return events, // not created yet: inferior not started
173:         };
174:         let mut reader = BufReader::new(file);
175:         if reader.seek(SeekFrom::Start(self.offset)).is_err() {
176:             return events;
177:         }
178:         let mut buffer = Vec::new();
179:         // The event file is bounded by the program's allocation count and
180:         // the engine's caps; read everything appended since last time.
181:         if reader.read_to_end(&mut buffer).is_err() {
182:             return events;
183:         }
184: 
185:         let mut data = std::mem::take(&mut self.partial);
186:         data.extend_from_slice(&buffer);
187:         let mut consumed = 0usize;
188:         let mut pos = 0usize;
189:         while pos < data.len() {
190:             match data[pos..].iter().position(|&b| b == b'\n') {
191:                 Some(nl) => {
192:                     let line = &data[pos..pos + nl];
193:                     consumed = pos + nl + 1;
194:                     pos += nl + 1;
195:                     if line.is_empty() {
196:                         continue;
197:                     }
198:                     match parse_event_line(&String::from_utf8_lossy(line)) {
199:                         Ok(ev) => events.push(ev),
200:                         Err(e) => {
201:                             if self.parse_errors.len() < 50 {
202:                                 self.parse_errors.push(e.to_string());
203:                             }
204:                         }
205:                     }
206:                 }
207:                 None => break, // incomplete line, keep for next call
208:             }
209:         }
210:         // Keep the unconsumed partial tail in memory; the file offset always
211:         // points past the bytes we have already READ (not parsed), so the
212:         // buffered partial is never re-read from disk.
213:         self.partial = data[consumed..].to_vec();
214:         self.offset += buffer.len() as u64;
215:         events
216:     }
217: }

Batched addr2line queries use\n+image-relative PCs, then map results back to raw PCs. Unsupported executable\n+formats, unknown modules and absent symbols stay unresolved.\n+\n+## Deadlines, processes and stage health\n+\n+`--timeout` starts before tool probes and bounds the entire pipeline via\n+`Instant`. Compiler/debugger/analysis budgets are each clamped to the same\n+deadline. Every GDB command—including snapshot queries—checks it and the\n+command cap. A successful `^running` acknowledgement is **not** a stop.\n+Late async tokens cannot resolve command oneshots. On response timeout the\n+session is poisoned rather than risking attribution of late streams.\n+\n+A missing-stop wait before the overall deadline is a debugger failure with\n+an operation reason, **not proof of an infinite loop**. Expiring the global\n+or stage deadline is a timeout. After expiry, new analyses are skipped.\n+Each stage records timing offsets/duration, native exit code when available,\n+failure reason, output completeness and partial-results availability.\n+Skipped stages have no fictitious start/exit timestamps.\n+\n+GCC, addr2line, Valgrind and sanitizer processes have cancellation-owned\n+groups and concurrent bounded pipe drains. Descendants cannot hold pipes\n+open forever. GDB and its separately grouped inferior are both terminated;\n+the interrupt request has a 100ms bound before forced termination/reaping.\n+Allow up to two seconds for process cleanup after a deadline.\n+\n+Inferior address-space/CPU/file/core limits are set with Linux `prlimit`\n+at the initial stop—not on GDB itself. Startup before that stop is outside\n+these inferior-only rlimits. Diagnostic runtimes have CPU/file/open-file\n+limits, **not** an ASan-breaking small virtual-address cap. `RLIMIT_NPROC`\n+is not used: it is per-user, not per-tree. A delegated cgroup adds\n+best-effort tree memory/PID control. Without one, descendants that deliberately\n+escape their group are not guaranteed contained.\n+These mechanisms are **not a security sandbox**.\n+\n+Malformed/missing Valgrind XML never produces a successful empty report.\n+Complete native `<error>` records can be recovered from a truncated file;\n+`output_complete`, `summary_available` and `parse_error` disambiguate absent\n+summary data from zero totals. Legacy integer summary fields keep their old\n+defaults for compatibility; **do not interpret them when `summary_available`\n+is false**. Sanitizers run independently, never under Valgrind, and nonzero\n+exits without diagnostics are inconclusive. Sanitizer fallback is recorded\n+in metadata/notes.\n+\n+## Storage and budgets\n+\n+JSON export streams directly to writers (stdout and optional file), avoiding\n+one enormous in-memory JSON string. `--journal file.jsonl` writes ordered,\n+independently parseable configuration, disassembly, register, checkpoint, gap\n+and instruction records as execution proceeds. Existing journal files are\n+never overwritten. A finalized footer is synced on successful closure.\n+`storage.finalized` says whether collection closed, **not** whether execution\n+completed or coverage was complete.\n+\n+`storage::recover` incrementally reads complete records and ignores a\n+crash-torn last line. `--journal-only` evicts dynamic instruction events from\n+resident output; the JSON index still contains tables and bounded source\n+snapshots. This is not a random-access binary/indexed storage format:\n+seeking a JSONL journal currently requires a scan.\n+\n+Limits terminate recording/execution rather than silently downgrade fidelity:\n+\n+| Configuration | Default | Meaning |\n+|---|---:|---|\n+| `max_instruction_events` | 100,000 | attempted instruction events |\n+| `max_source_checkpoints` | 1,000 | source-state records; also clamped to legacy max snapshots |\n+| `max_gdb_commands` | 1,000,000 | all debugger queries and execution commands |\n+| `max_trace_bytes` | 128 MiB | serialized journal data budget (also counted without a journal) |\n+| `max_trace_memory_bytes` | 32 MiB | serialized resident-record accounting, not total Rust RSS |\n+| `max_register_snapshot_bytes` | 64 KiB | one register observation |\n+| `max_globals` | 32 | global/static inspection expressions |\n+| `compiler_timeout_seconds` | 30 | compiler stage, clamped to whole session |\n+| `debugger_timeout_seconds` | 30 | debugger stage, clamped to whole session |\n+| `analysis_timeout_seconds` | 10 | each analysis, clamped to whole session |\n+\n+Legacy max steps counts source steps in source mode, checkpoint progression\n+in dual mode; instruction budgets are separate. Export formatting, compatibility\n+arrays, heap summaries and control metadata can exceed journal byte accounting;\n+the cap is **not** a hard final-JSON file-size or engine-RSS limit. Source\n+snapshots/static tables remain resident under their accounting caps even with\n+journal-only capture. More compact indexed storage and hard engine-RSS\n+supervision are future work.\n+\n+## Configuration example\n+\n+```json\n+{\n+  \"source\": \"sample.c\",\n+  \"limits\": {\n+    \"timeout_seconds\": 20,\n+    \"debugger_timeout_seconds\": 15,\n+    \"max_instruction_events\": 5000,\n+    \"max_source_checkpoints\": 500,\n+    \"max_trace_memory_bytes\": 16777216\n+  },\n+  \"tracing\": {\n+    \"mode\": \"dual\",\n+    \"registers\": true,\n+    \"static_disassembly\": true,\n+    \"register_checkpoint_interval\": 256,\n+    \"memory_regions\": [{\"address\": \"&global_value\", \"size\": 4}],\n+    \"globals\": [\"function::local_static\"],\n+    \"discover_globals\": true,\n+    \"journal\": \"session.jsonl\",\n+    \"retain_instruction_events\": false,\n+    \"profiling\": true\n+  }\n+}\n+```\n+\n+Use expressions that exist in your own program. Relative source/include paths\n+are evaluated against the configured build working directory.\n+Configuration enums reject unsupported tracing modes; no silent fidelity downgrade.\n+\n+## Validation and measurements\n+\n+See `tests/v2.rs`, transport/parser unit tests, legacy integrations, and\n+[benchmark measurements](benchmarks.md). New coverage includes null writes\n+at the fault PC, both source and instruction infinite-loop deadlines, callbacks,\n+recursion, same-line functions, globals/statics, pointer-to-pointer links, PIE,\n+address reuse, moving realloc, missing source mappings, output caps, selected\n+memory, register replay, malformed/truncated records, GDB death and cleanup,\n+journal recovery, and instruction limits.\n+\n+The recorder supports Linux/GDB MI targets; relocation normalization is\n+currently ELF64 little-endian. No globally atomic cross-process snapshots,\n+complete multi-thread/fork instruction timeline, self-modifying/JIT fidelity,\n+all-library tracing, full lexical DWARF identity, or omniscient instruction\n+memory history is claimed.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

206:         return; /* passive mode: wrappers pass through, nothing recorded */
207:     g_fd = open(path, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_APPEND | O_CLOEXEC, 0600);
208: }
209: 
210: __attribute__((destructor(101)))
211: static void cte_fini(void)
212: {
213:     if (g_fd >= 0) {
214:         close(g_fd);
215:         g_fd = -1;
216:     }
217: }
218: 
219: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
220: /* Wrapped allocation functions                                        */
221: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
222: 
223: void *__wrap_malloc(size_t size)
224: {
225:     void *ret = __real_malloc(size);
226:     if (g_busy)
227:         return ret;
228:     g_busy = 1;
229:     unsigned long caller = (unsigned long)__builtin_return_address(0);
230:     cte_lock();
231:     unsigned long id = ++g_ids;
232:     cte_emit_locked("malloc", id, (unsigned long)ret, size, 0, 0, caller,
233:                     ret ? "ok" : "failed");
234:     if (ret)
235:         cte_insert((unsigned long)ret, id, size);
236:     cte_unlock();
237:     g_busy = 0;
238:     return ret;
239: }
240: 
241: void *__wrap_calloc(size_t nmemb, size_t size)
242: {
243:     void *ret = __real_calloc(nmemb, size);
244:     if (g_busy)
245:         return ret;
246:     g_busy = 1;
247:     unsigned long caller = (unsigned long)__builtin_return_address(0);
248:     /* The wrapped product mirrors the ABI; the real calloc validates
249:      * overflow itself (returns NULL), which we record as "failed". */
250:     unsigned long total = nmemb * size;
251:     cte_lock();
252:     unsigned long id = ++g_ids;
253:     cte_emit_locked("calloc", id, (unsigned long)ret, total, 0, 0, caller,
254:                     ret ? "ok" : "failed");
255:     if (ret)
256:         cte_insert((unsigned long)ret, id, total);
257:     cte_unlock();
258:     g_busy = 0;
259:     return ret;
260: }
261: 
262: void *__wrap_realloc(void *ptr, size_t size)
263: {
264:     void *ret = __real_realloc(ptr, size);
265:     if (g_busy)
266:         return ret;
267:     g_busy = 1;
268:     unsigned long caller = (unsigned long)__builtin_return_address(0);
269: 
270:     cte_lock();
271:     cte_slot *slot = ptr ? cte_find((unsigned long)ptr) : NULL;
272:     unsigned long old_id = slot ? slot->id : 0;
273:     unsigned long id;
274:     const char *status;
275:     if (ptr == NULL) {
276:         id = ++g_ids;
277:         status = "new"; /* realloc(NULL, n) == malloc(n) */
278:     } else if (ret == ptr) {
279:         id = old_id;
280:         status = "ok_same"; /* in-place growth/shrink: id stays stable */
281:     } else if (ret != NULL) {
282:         id = ++g_ids;
283:         status = "ok_moved"; /* old block retired, new id for new address */
284:     } else if (size == 0) {
285:         id = old_id;
286:         status = "zero"; /* glibc: realloc(p, 0) frees p and returns NULL */
287:     } else {
288:         id = old_id;
289:         status = "failed"; /* original allocation preserved */
290:     }
291:     cte_emit_locked("realloc", id, (unsigned long)ret, size, old_id,
292:                     (unsigned long)ptr, caller, status);
293: 
294:     /* Table maintenance (never before emission, and state changes must
295:      * match what the real allocator actually did). */
296:     if (ptr != NULL) {
297:         if (ret == ptr)
298:             slot->size = size; /* id stable, size updated */
299:         else if (ret != NULL || size == 0)
300:             cte_remove((unsigned long)ptr);
301:         /* status == "failed": keep the original entry */
302:     }
303:     if (ret != NULL && (ptr == NULL || ret != ptr))
304:         cte_insert((unsigned long)ret, id, size);
305:     cte_unlock();
306:     g_busy = 0;
307:     return ret;
308: }
309: 
310: void __wrap_free(void *ptr)
311: {
312:     if (g_busy) {
313:         __real_free(ptr);
314:         return;
315:     }
316:     g_busy = 1;
317:     unsigned long caller = (unsigned long)__builtin_return_address(0);
318:     __real_free(ptr);
319:     cte_lock();
320:     cte_slot *slot = ptr ? cte_find((unsigned long)ptr) : NULL;
321:     unsigned long id = slot ? slot->id : 0;
322:     const char *status = ptr ? (slot ? "ok" : "unknown") : "null";
323:     unsigned long size = slot ? slot->size : 0;
324:     cte_emit_locked("free", id, (unsigned long)ptr, size, 0, 0, caller, status);
325:     if (slot)
326:         cte_remove((unsigned long)ptr);
327:     cte_unlock();
328:     g_busy = 0;
329: }

_Thinking:_

**Fixing pointer lifetime**

The allocation-runtime audit found two more correctness bugs. Its “passive” mode still retained pointers in the tracking table, which could make Valgrind report a genuine leak as merely reachable. Also, an in-place `realloc` of an untracked pointer could dereference a missing table entry.

I’m fixing both before generating the final examples. The benchmark samples are recorded; I’ll rerun them after these runtime changes so the report matches the final code.

123:   Valgrind (XML)     sanitized run        addr2line batch
124:   memcheck report    (crash pass only)    (caller file:line resolution)
125:         └───────────────────┴────────────────────┘
126:                             ▼
127:                      DebugSessionTrace (JSON)
128: ```
129: 
130: 1. **Build** (`compiler.rs`): every translation unit is compiled with `-g -O0`
131:    plus GCC's machine-readable diagnostics (`sarif-stderr` first, with
132:    fallbacks for older GCC), linked with a small C runtime that intercepts
133:    `malloc/calloc/realloc/free` via `-Wl,--wrap=...` and appends one event
134:    line per operation to a dedicated trace file. A second, sanitizer-built
135:    binary (ASan, plus UBSan when installed) is produced for the crash
136:    diagnostic pass; if a sanitizer runtime is missing the engine degrades
137:    and records a note.
138: 2. **Execute** (`gdb_mi.rs`, `trace.rs`): the debug binary runs under GDB in
139:    MI2 mode with a token-matched command/response layer and a dedicated pty
140:    for program output. The engine breaks at `main`, single-steps in user
141:    code, and `finish`es out of non-user frames. At every stop it captures
142:    one snapshot: call stack, variables (own address, pointed-to address,
143:    raw bytes), live heap block contents read through GDB within the
144:    per-snapshot memory budget, and the program output so far.
145: 3. **Heap reconstruction** (`allocation_tracker.rs`): the event file is
146:    ingested into a timeline that reconstructs every allocation, its caller,
147:    realloc chains and its final status; `addr2line` resolves caller PCs to
148:    `file:line` in one batched call.
149: 4. **Independent analyses**: Valgrind runs the program separately (its XML
150:    parsed with `roxmltree`, findings correlated with allocation ids by
151:    file/line). On a crash, the sanitized binary runs once as a diagnostic
152:    pass and its report is attached to the crash report.
153: 
154: Partial results are always preserved: a timeout, step limit or crash yields
155: a trace with everything captured up to that point.
156: 
157: Traces emit `schema_version: 2` and `stage_results` to distinguish completed,
158: failed, timed-out, and skipped analyses. Older trace JSON without these fields
159: remains deserializable; absent stage metadata is unknown, not a clean result.
160: 
161: ## Resource limits
162: 
163: | Flag | Default | Enforced by |
164: |------|---------|-------------|
165: | `--max-steps` | 1000 | engine step loop |
166: | `--timeout` (s) | 10 | monotonic whole-session deadline, including compilation and analysis |
167: | `--max-memory-mb` | 256 | traced program's address space (engine budget model) |
168: | `--max-output-bytes` | 1048576 | program output head capture; terminate on exhaustion |
169: | `--max-heap-allocations` | 10000 | timeline |
170: | `--max-snapshots` | 1000 | snapshot list |
171: | `--max-snapshot-memory-bytes` | 1048576 | variables + heap reads per snapshot |
172: | `--max-memory-read-bytes` | 4096 | one `-data-read-memory-bytes` call |
173: | `--max-processes` | 16 | cgroup v2 `pids.max` (best effort) |
174: | `--max-variables` | 24 | per-snapshot introspection |
175: 
176: **These limits are not a security sandbox.** They protect the *engine and
177: the user session* from runaway programs; a hostile binary can still do harm
178: on the host machine. Real isolation needs a container or VM.
179: 
180: Platform notes: Linux `RLIMIT_NPROC` is per real user id, not per process
181: tree, so it is deliberately not used (it would break GDB's own spawning on
182: a normal desktop session). Process-tree caps work only when a delegated
183: cgroup v2 subtree is available; otherwise the engine keeps rlimits for CPU
184: and file size and says so in `analysis_notes`.
185: 
186: ## CLI > config file > defaults
187: 
188: Scalar flags override the JSON config file; list flags (`--define`,
189: `--compiler-flag`, …) **append** to the file's lists. See
190: [`docs/build-config.md`](docs/build-config.md) for the exact field mapping
191: (the file is the same shape the future GUI will edit).
192: 
193: ## Limitations & known deviations
194: 
195: * `--wrap` instrumentation covers the program's own allocator calls; memory
196:   allocated *inside* libc/other shared libraries is invisible to the
197:   timeline (Valgrind still sees it all — it is the independent check).
198: * A freed block's raw bytes are the **last bytes captured while it was
199:   alive**; freed memory contents are not read after the fact.
200: * The sanitized pass is ASan-only when libubsan is not installed (the
201:   engine notes this in `analysis_notes`).
202: * Program output and GDB console chatter are kept separate (pty); the
203:   MI-facing `@` target stream is treated as program output for GDB versions
204:   without tty support.
205: * Snapshots are line-level: multiple stops on the same line are collapsed
206:   by the step budget, not deduplicated.
207: 
208: ## Development
209: 
210: ```sh
211: cargo test --lib      # unit tests; one live GDB lifecycle regression skips if absent
212: cargo test --test integration   # full pipeline against real gcc/gdb/valgrind
213: cargo test --test v2 -- --test-threads=1  # dual-level and reliability regressions
214: python3 scripts/benchmark.py            # build first; three serial samples per case
215: ```
216: 
217: The integration suite skips gracefully (with a printed reason) when a tool
218: is missing. Layout: `src/` modules mirror the pipeline stages; `c_runtime/`
219: holds the embedded C tracking runtime; `fixtures/c/` one deliberate bug per
220: file for manual and automated testing.
221: 
222: License: MIT.

160: 
161: ## 6. Resource controls (`resource_limits.rs`)
162: 
163: Layered enforcement:
164: 
165: 1. **Engine clocks** — wall deadline, per-command and per-step timeouts;
166:    every path is bounded, verified with real GDB.
167: 2. **rlimits** — `RLIMIT_CPU` (from `timeout_seconds`), `RLIMIT_FSIZE`,
168:    `RLIMIT_NOFILE` on sanitizer/valgrind children. `RLIMIT_NPROC` is
169:    deliberately never used: on Linux it is enforced per *real user id*, so
170:    a low value breaks every `fork` on the whole desktop session
171:    (empirically: `vfork: Resource temporarily unavailable` with 173 user
172:    processes).
173: 3. **cgroup v2** — when a delegated subtree is writable, the inferior pid
174:    is moved into it with `pids.max`, `memory.max` and `cpu.max`; on teardown
175:    the subtree is killed (`cgroup.kill`). Best effort; its availability is
176:    reported in `session_meta.cgroup_enforced`.
177: 
178: These limits protect the engine and the session — they are **not a
179: security sandbox** for hostile binaries.

1: # V2 recording contract
2: 
3: ## Architecture and compatibility
4: 
5: The existing GCC pipeline, MI tokenizer/parser, allocation runtime, native
6: Valgrind XML parser and sanitizer parser are reused. `trace.rs` coordinates
7: stages and the stop loop; `recorder.rs` captures and journals observations;
8: `processor.rs` validates references and reconstructs recorded register deltas.
9: `supervisor.rs` owns monotonic budgets and cancellation-safe child groups.
10: 
11: The wire schema is **2**. Existing fields (`snapshots`, `heap_events`,
12: `execution_status`, reports, metadata) remain. New fields include:
13: 
14: - `execution`: canonical typed program outcome, exit code, signal, crash PC.
15: - `stage_results`: independent compiler/debugger/Valgrind/sanitizer/tracker health.
16: - `tracing_configuration`, `coverage`, `storage`, `profiling`.
17: - `execution_limits`: the effective limits used for the recording.
18: - `disassembly_table`, `instruction_events`, `initial_registers`, `trace_gaps`.
19: - `source_checkpoints`: indices into `snapshots`, not duplicate memory objects.
20: - `allocation_lifetimes`: stable IDs, native event sequence boundaries, raw
21:   caller PCs, module and explicit resolved/unresolved status.
22: 
23: Legacy fields are not renamed: for example `execution_status: "timeout"`
24: corresponds to `execution.outcome: "timed_out"`. Recording/output caps use the
25: legacy `step_limit_reached` alias; `execution.outcome` distinguishes output
26: exhaustion. A Valgrind failure does not change the program outcome.
27: Old documents deserialize with default V2 extension fields; absence of those
28: fields is **not evidence that instruction recording occurred**.
29: 
30: Consumers can continue using legacy snapshots, or navigate V2 references.
31: Validate with `processor::validate`. In journal-only mode load instruction
32: records from the journal: an empty resident array does not mean zero events.
33: 
34: ## Timeline semantics (avoid the PC off-by-one)
35: 
36: At stop S, GDB's PC identifies the **next** instruction. The recorder:
37: 
38: 1. Observes that address/source/thread.
39: 2. Sends `-exec-step-instruction` and separately awaits async `*stopped`.
40: 3. Emits an event containing the **pre-attempt** address and the observed
41:    `next_address`, post-attempt stop reason, registers and selected memory.
42: 
43: `event_id` is zero-based, ordered, and counts **attempts**, not just successful
44: instructions. `outcome` is:
45: 
46: - `completed`: GDB reported the single-step completion.
47: - `faulted`: a synchronous fault signal stopped at the attempted PC.
48: - `interrupted`: another signal interrupted execution.
49: - `unknown`: no sufficient completion evidence, including failed/missing stops.
50: 
51: Breakpoint stops are conservatively not treated as proof of completion.
52: No event is generated by disassembly alone.
53: 
54: `stop_id_before/after` connect events to actual observed stops; an absent
55: after-stop ID means no response was observed. Snapshots contain
56: `observation.stop_id`, PC, thread, PID, origin, errors, and
57: `instruction_position`: the number of recorded attempts before that snapshot.
58: Position 0 is before the first attempt; position N is after N attempts.
59: `checkpoint_id` references the most recent source checkpoint, not a claim
60: that its memory still equals the current memory.
61: 
62: Source checkpoints occur at initial entry, file/line/function changes,
63: entry breakpoints, and faults. Repeated loop iterations remain separate
64: events. Same-line function changes are preserved. A native exit without a
65: source frame is represented by the execution outcome and ending gap, not an
66: invented variable snapshot.
67: 
68: ## Coverage
69: 
70: The supported instruction scope is **user code**. Frame origins are
71: `user_code`, `instrumentation_runtime`, `system_library`, or `unknown`.
72: Allocator/runtime frames do not become ordinary source checkpoints, but
73: allocation events still enter the timeline before the next checkpoint.
74: 
75: Gaps identify startup and each interval skipped by source stepping or
76: `finish`/`continue` through excluded code. A gap has a boundary position and
77: observed endpoint PCs; its unknown instruction count is never guessed.
78: User entry-address breakpoints (bounded discovery of 128 functions) make
79: callbacks such as `qsort` observable inside skipped library calls. Missing
80: DWARF mappings, capped discovery and native debugger limitations can still
81: limit coverage. No all-libraries or all-process instruction-capture mode is
82: claimed.
83: 
84: The backend reports GDB **all-stop** mode. Multiple observed threads mark
85: instruction coverage incomplete: this version records selected-thread steps,
86: not a complete interleaving. All-stop does not freeze external processes
87: sharing memory. Fork children are not instruction-traced; allocation events
88: may still arrive from them. Entry capture does not trace the dynamic loader
89: before main.
90: 
91: ## Registers
92: 
93: GDB register names/numbers and target architecture text are retained; no
94: x86-specific register indices are hard-coded. Initial and periodic full
95: observations establish delta bases. For each step, a full native GDB query
96: is compared with the previous **observed** register set for that thread.
97: Only changed values are serialized between checkpoints. Missing values
98: explicitly invalidate older ones; they never become zero.
99: 
100: The default full-checkpoint interval is 256 attempts. A gap forces the next
101: observation to be full. A capped or failed register read cannot establish
102: a valid new base. `processor::replay_registers` seeks the latest valid full
103: checkpoint and applies deltas; it errors rather than returning stale values
104: as exact when observations are missing. It operates on resident events;
105: journal readers can implement the same rule incrementally.
106: 
107: Disassembly is collected in bounded 128-byte windows and cached per loaded-image epoch, with runtime addresses,
108: native bytes/text, function and module mapping. Library load/unload
109: notifications invalidate the address cache without invalidating old table
110: IDs. ASLR addresses are never replaced with fake addresses.
111: Self-modifying/JIT code is **unsupported**; immutable code is a requirement
112: for cache fidelity.
113: 
114: ## Memory and value validity
115: 
116: Rich memory is captured at source checkpoints while stopped. Individual
117: values distinguish `valid`, `unavailable`, `unreadable`, `optimized_out`,
118: `truncated`, and `not_captured`. Here “valid” means the debugger returned
119: an observation, **not** proof of C initialization or absence of undefined
120: behavior. No uninitialized state is inferred from byte patterns.
121: 
122: Pointers retain their exact `address` (pointer storage) and `points_to`
123: (stored target). `target` classification uses recorded extents/symbols:
124: null, heap (ID/base/offset/active), known stack variables, globals/statics,
125: or unknown. Code/stack/unmapped classifications can additionally use actual
126: `/proc/PID/maps` evidence; failure to read mappings stays unknown.
127: Extent matches describe address evidence, not pointer provenance: address
128: reuse cannot prove whether a pointer originated from an old object.

137: storage-based fallback IDs are explicit; ambiguous associations omit addresses
138: instead of guessing. No Python code executes inside the C inferior.
139: Raw DWARF DIE IDs and non-top-frame local inspection remain unsupported.
140: Storage classifications use observed Linux mappings and remain unknown when
141: evidence is insufficient.
142: Global/file-static symbols are discovered through MI, with file qualification
143: for ambiguity. Function-local statics become persistent inspection expressions
144: once observed in their function; `--global 'function::name'` can request them
145: earlier.
146: 
147: Variables, heap and globals share the source snapshot byte budget. Optional
148: `--memory-region '&global_value:4'` records bounded **actual reads after each
149: instruction stop**, with expression, resolved address, bytes and status.
150: Without such an observation, instruction-position memory is **last-known**
151: from an earlier checkpoint or unavailable, never exact by implication.
152: No assembly interpretation or synthetic write reconstruction is used.
153: Inspection function calls are disabled; side-effect expressions are rejected.
154: 
155: Heap event ordering is ingestion order: drain telemetry while the inferior
156: is stopped, then read source state. A snapshot records the number of
157: ingested heap events. Native sequence numbers remain per-process; IDs widen
158: with PID when multiple processes are observed. Realloc-in-place preserves an

160: object. Linker wrapping does not see internal allocations in shared libraries.
