1: //! Ordered recoverable JSONL journal. Each complete line is independently parseable.
2: use crate::error::Result;
3: use serde::Serialize;
4: use std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};
5: use std::io::Write;
6: use std::path::Path;
7: 
8: pub struct Journal {
9:     file: Option<File>,
10:     pub bytes: u64,
11:     cap: usize,
12: }
13: impl Journal {
14:     pub fn new(path: Option<&Path>, cap: usize) -> Result<Self> {
15:         // Never overwrite an existing trace or user file.
16:         let file = path
17:             .map(|p| OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true).open(p))
18:             .transpose()?;
19:         Ok(Self {
20:             file,
21:             bytes: 0,
22:             cap,
23:         })
24:     }
25:     pub fn append(&mut self, kind: &str, value: &impl Serialize) -> Result<usize> {
26:         #[derive(Serialize)]
27:         struct Record<'a, T> {
28:             kind: &'a str,
29:             data: &'a T,
30:         }
31:         let record = Record { kind, data: value };
32:         let mut bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&record)?;
33:         bytes.push(b'\n');
34:         if self.bytes.saturating_add(bytes.len() as u64) > self.cap as u64 {
35:             return Err(crate::error::EngineError::LimitReached("max_trace_bytes"));
36:         }
37:         if let Some(file) = &mut self.file {
38:             file.write_all(&bytes)?;
39:             // File (not BufWriter): completed records are visible even on interruption.
40:         }
41:         self.bytes += bytes.len() as u64;
42:         Ok(bytes.len())
43:     }
44:     pub fn finalize(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
45:         // Finalization footer is control metadata, allowed beyond the data budget.
46:         if let Some(file) = &mut self.file {
47:             file.write_all(b"{\"kind\":\"finalized\",\"data\":true}\n")?;
48:             file.sync_data()?;
49:         }
50:         Ok(())
51:     }
52: }
53: 
54: /// Recover complete records incrementally; a crash-torn last line is ignored.
55: pub fn recover(path: &Path) -> Result<impl Iterator<Item = Result<serde_json::Value>>> {
56:     use std::io::{BufRead, Read};
57:     let mut reader = std::io::BufReader::new(File::open(path)?);
58:     Ok(std::iter::from_fn(move || {
59:         let mut line = Vec::new();
60:         let result = (&mut reader)
61:             .take(16 * 1024 * 1024)
62:             .read_until(b'\n', &mut line);
63:         match result {
64:             Ok(0) => None,
65:             Ok(_) if line.last() != Some(&b'\n') => None,
66:             Ok(_) => Some(serde_json::from_slice(&line).map_err(Into::into)),
67:             Err(e) => Some(Err(e.into())),
68:         }
69:     }))
70: }

The checkpoint context will expose that boundary explicitly, while event-to-checkpoint joins will use the recorded `checkpoint_id`. Evidence references will be typed positions tied to one store, not runtime IDs or globally reusable numbers.

A raw consumer never depends on a semantic consumer.\n+\n+```rust\n+use c_trace_engine::trace_parser::{\n+    Evidence, EvidenceLocation, TraceLoadOptions, TraceStore,\n+};\n+\n+let store = TraceStore::open(\"examples/v21_dual.json\", TraceLoadOptions::default())?;\n+let raw = store.raw();\n+let events = raw.instruction_range(0..5)?; // half-open borrowed slice\n+let entry = raw.disassembly_for_event(0)?;\n+let semantic = store.semantic_input();\n+let context = semantic.source_checkpoint_context(0)?;\n+let original = semantic.resolve_evidence(&context.snapshot_evidence()?)?;\n+assert!(matches!(original, Evidence::Snapshot(_)));\n+let event_ref = raw.evidence_ref(EvidenceLocation::InstructionEvent(0))?;\n+assert!(matches!(semantic.resolve_evidence(&event_ref)?, Evidence::InstructionEvent(_)));\n+# let _ = (events, entry);\n+# Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())\n+```\n+\n+### Checkpoint context and availability\n+\n+`checkpoint_context(snapshot_index)` borrows **any** retained snapshot;\n+`source_checkpoint_context(position)` follows the *explicit* list and also\n+reports `Some(position)` as the path by which it was obtained. An ordinary\n+snapshot context's `source_checkpoint_position()` is `None` meaning\n+**unasserted**, not proof the snapshot is absent from the list.\n+`semantic.snapshots()` iterates *all* snapshots in order; the separate\n+`semantic.source_checkpoints()` iterates the journaled list in its original\n+order, including repeated positions if present, and returns errors for bad\n+entries. Both traversals are O(1) per context, with no temporary vectors.\n+\n+`CheckpointContext` borrows the original snapshot, frames, local variables,\n+globals and heap-block observations. It exposes optional source `(file,line)`\n+and optional one-based GDB stop id; legacy/default empty file/zero line and\n+zero stop are **not** upgraded into identities. No O(E) scan is hidden in\n+sequential checkpoint traversal.\n+\n+### Typed evidence references\n+\n+`EvidenceLocation` distinguishes original positions in snapshots, instruction\n+events, disassembly, heap events/final state/lifetimes, gaps, compiler\n+diagnostics, internal diagnostics, structured Valgrind errors, optional\n+reports, and nested frame/variable/global/heap-block/memory observations.\n+`store.evidence_ref(location)` validates the position *before* creating a\n+small `EvidenceRef`; `store.resolve_evidence(&reference)` returns a typed\n+borrowed `Evidence<'_>`. Allocation IDs\n+and stop counters are runtime identities, not evidence positions.\n+\n+### TP-3 performance and cache decision (release, 2026-11-16)\n+\n+`cargo run --release --example trace_parser_tp3_bench -- TRACE.json [...]`\n+measures parse and TP-2 indexing separately, then runs **seven rounds** per\n+TP-3 operation, reporting median / nearest-rank p95 (maximum of seven\n+samples). `black_box` consumes varying positional queries; a counting\n+allocator reports live bytes and allocation calls. ## Assistant

_Thinking:_

**Checks weak trace identity**

_Thinking:_

**Checking documentation counts**

**TP-3 is implemented. Verdict: PASS for the shared trace-access foundation, with a WARNING about existing timing-sensitive debugger tests and incomplete Stage 1 evidence.** No Semantic Engine or GUI work was added.

## A. Repository findings

TP-3 reuses TP-1’s canonical `Arc<DebugSessionTrace>` and ingestion API, plus TP-2’s shared `Arc<TraceIndexes>`, borrowed queries, and explicit `validate_deep()`. Complete V2.1 JSON remains authoritative; journal parsing remains record-only.

## B. Architecture

`store.raw()` and `store.semantic_input()` each create a one-reference borrowed view of the **same** `TraceStore`. The raw view delegates existing TP-2 queries; the semantic-input view organizes recorded observations without interpreting C semantics. Neither reparses, copies the trace, or builds an index.

## C. Implementation

| Files | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `src/trace_parser/views.rs` | Both views, checkpoint contexts, ordered traversal |
| `src/trace_parser/evidence.rs` | Trace-scoped typed evidence references and resolution |
| `src/trace_parser/mod.rs`, `error.rs` | Public exports, view constructors, `ForeignTrace` error |
| `tests/trace_parser_views.rs` | Nine focused TP-3 integration tests |
| `examples/trace_parser_tp3_bench.rs` | Reproducible release benchmark |
| `docs/trace-parser.md`, `README.md` | Finished architecture, semantics, performance, limitations |

Stage 1 recording and journal-writing code were not changed.

## D. Public API

```rust
let raw = store.raw();
let events = raw.instruction_range(0..5)?;
let assembly = raw.disassembly_for_event(0)?;

let semantic = store.semantic_input();
let context = semantic.source_checkpoint_context(0)?;
let reference = context.snapshot_evidence()?;
let original = semantic.resolve_evidence(&reference)?;
```

`RawTraceView` exposes existing `TraceStore` queries through delegation. `SemanticInputView` adds `checkpoint_context`, `source_checkpoint_context`, ordered `snapshots()` and `source_checkpoints()` iterators, and evidence access.

## E. Observation context

A `CheckpointContext` borrows the original snapshot, frames, variables, globals, and heap blocks. It exposes recorded source and stop identity, attempted instruction position, completeness, coverage, and explicitly checkpoint-tagged event ranges. Its heap query returns a **retained-snapshot boundary interval**, not a claim that every event happened at that exact stop. Missing relationships remain unavailable; no nearest-event join is made.

## F. Evidence model

`EvidenceLocation` distinguishes snapshot, instruction-event, disassembly, heap, gap, diagnostic, report, and nested observation positions. `evidence_ref()` validates a position; `resolve_evidence()` returns the canonical borrowed record. References carry a weak trace identity: store clones can resolve them, but an independently loaded trace—even identical JSON—returns `QueryError::ForeignTrace`. Allocation IDs and GDB stop counters are never treated as evidence positions.

## G. Memory and ownership

Each view is one pointer wide. Release instrumentation measured **0 additional persistent bytes and 0 allocation calls** for view creation; repeated single-threaded context, traversal, evidence, range, and source queries also counted zero allocations. Parallel benchmark allocation counts came from spawning and joining threads, not the queries. References do not own the trace.

## H. Performance

On the Intel Pentium 3558U release benchmark, seven rounds per operation gave:

| Operation | Dual trace median / p95 | 94,306-event trace median / p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Either view creation | ~2 / 2–3 ns | ~2 / 2–3 ns |
| Varied checkpoint context | 12.9 / 16.1 ns | 12.8 / 13.0 ns |
| Evidence resolution | 33.2 / 75.6 ns | 33.3 / 37.5 ns |
| Bounded instruction range | 13.0 / 13.3 ns | 13.0 / 13.3 ns |

Traversing **1,000** source checkpoints took 5.99 µs median; traversing them with checkpoint-event queries took 13.37 µs. Parse and TP-2 build costs were measured separately. No query cache was justified or added. Methodology, additional fixtures, and limitations are in `docs/trace-parser.md`.

## I. Testing

`cargo test -- --test-threads=1`: **194 passed, 0 failed**. A separate default-parallel `cargo test` also passed all 194. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check` pass.

One earlier parallel library run failed an existing supervisor test that cancels after a fixed 100 ms while assuming child output has already arrived; its isolated rerun passed. Cross-binary debugger subprocess load and short deadlines remain a harness reliability risk, documented separately. TP-3 did not alter the process supervisor.

## J. Known limitations

Journals cannot reconstruct finalized complete traces. Historical V2 traces can still encounter the pre-existing model-field compatibility limitation. Missing source mappings, unreadable bytes, skipped tools, retention gaps, and coarse heap-stop attribution remain explicit. Evidence references are in-process and trace-local, not serializable cross-session IDs.

## K. Stage 2 readiness

**Ready as an observation-access foundation.** Stage 2 can consume recorded activation/scope metadata, stack frames, variable types and bytes, heap identities and realloc links, pointer metadata, diagnostic reports, and trace-local evidence references.

Stage 1 does **not** guarantee complete DWARF identity, every memory value at every checkpoint, exact heap-event-to-instruction attribution, full per-instruction registers, or complete observations on partial runs. Object identities, typed layouts, pointer relationships, checkpoint comparisons, lifetimes, and evidence-backed explanations therefore require Stage 2 interpretation with uncertainty preserved—not parser inference.

## L. Final verdict

**PASS — TP-3 access layer. WARNING — recorded-evidence limits and existing timing-sensitive debugger tests.**

## User

# VISUAL C — STAGE 1 EVIDENCE & METADATA AUDIT
## Comprehensive Technical Audit Before Stage 1 Enhancements

### Your role

Act as a senior Rust systems engineer, compiler-tooling engineer, and debugging-infrastructure architect.

You are auditing the existing **Visual C** project, an offline-first educational C debugging and memory-visualization application.

**This assignment is strictly an audit. Do not implement improvements, refactor the architecture, change schemas, or begin the Semantic Engine.**

Your objective is to determine how we can improve the accuracy, completeness, and usefulness of Stage 1 execution evidence before building Stage 2.

The final report must be grounded in actual repository code, actual recorded traces, and reproducible experiments.

Do not claim capabilities based solely on the presence of a library or compiler flag.

---

# 1. Existing project architecture

Visual C currently consists of two major implemented components.

## Stage 1 — C Trace Engine V2.1

A Rust-based execution recorder that uses:

- GCC to compile C programs with debugging information.
- GDB using MI2 to record execution.
- A structured tokenizer and parser for GDB/MI2 messages.
- Source-level checkpoints and variable observations.
- Executed assembly instruction events.
- Cached static disassembly.
- Allocation instrumentation for `malloc`, `calloc`, `realloc`, and `free`.
- Valgrind reporting.
- ASan/UBSan diagnostics.
- Execution limits and subprocess cleanup.
- JSON and journal trace output.

The existing recorder deliberately removed continuous CPU-register polling in V2.1 for performance reasons.

**Do not propose restoring continuous register polling by default.**

## Trace Parser — TP-1, TP-2, TP-3

A shared Rust component already implemented and tested.

Its architecture includes:

- Canonical `Arc<DebugSessionTrace>` ownership.
- JSON ingestion and structural validation.
- Compact indexes.
- Efficient borrowed queries.
- Cross-record resolution.
- Deep validation.
- `RawTraceView`.
- `SemanticInputView`.
- Checkpoint observation contexts.
- Trace-scoped evidence references.

The parser provides two access paths over one authoritative trace.

```text
Stage 1 Recorder
       |
       v
Recorded Execution Trace
       |
       v
Canonical TraceStore
       |
       +--------------------+
       |                    |
       v                    v
 RawTraceView       SemanticInputView
       |                    |
       v                    v
 Future GUI         Future Semantic
 Query API               Engine
```

The Trace Parser is considered functionally complete as a shared access foundation.

The upcoming Stage 2 Semantic Engine will use its recorded observations to construct memory objects, relationships, state differences, timelines, and educational diagnostics.

**We are auditing Stage 1 now because Stage 2 must not be designed around unnecessarily incomplete execution evidence.**

---

# 2. Our architectural decisions

Treat the following as project requirements.

1. **Keep GCC as the primary compiler.** We want to retain compatibility with GCC-specific syntax, GNU C extensions, and existing compilation behavior.

2. **Preserve GDB/MI2.** The existing tokenizer and parser should continue handling runtime debugger communication.

3. **Prioritize optimizing existing machinery before introducing new libraries or analysis systems.**

4. **Investigate `gimli` + `object`** as a possible Rust-native way to extract more DWARF debugging metadata from GCC-produced binaries.

5. **Consider Clang AST as an optional enrichment source**, not a second authoritative compiler or execution engine.

6. **Do not build a custom C interpreter.** Its implementation and maintenance complexity would likely outweigh its benefits for this project.

7. **Prefer small, evidence-grounded recognition patterns** for narrowly defined C constructs where useful, rather than implementing general C expression evaluation.

8. **Keep JSON as the trace format.** We are willing to extend the existing schema with additive metadata and explicit unavailable-value representations.

9. **Avoid unnecessary schema-version complexity.** Preserve compatibility where possible, and use version changes only where the format contract actually requires them.

10. **Prioritize educational accuracy and useful memory information over aggressive trace-size optimization.** However, preserve execution deadlines, resource limits, and bounded debugger work.

11. **Do not fabricate missing runtime evidence.** AST and DWARF can supplement static metadata but cannot replace measurements from actual execution.

12. **Develop improvements incrementally after the audit.** Each future implementation phase will be separately reviewed and tested.

# 11. Investigate optional Clang AST enrichment

We are considering Clang AST only as an additional source of **static source-code metadata**.

GCC remains authoritative for actual compilation and execution.

Do not replace GCC or integrate Clang yet.

### Investigate possible benefits

Assess whether Clang AST can provide information missing from current GCC/DWARF evidence, including:

- Exact declaration identities.
- Shadowed declarations.
- Variable initialization expressions.
- `malloc`/`calloc`/`realloc` call expressions.
- Allocation-size expressions.
- Array indexing expressions.
- Pointer arithmetic expressions.
- Dereference expressions.
- Address-of expressions.
- Struct field accesses.
- Assignment expressions.
- Function call structure.
- Source-level control flow.

### Example

```c
int *p = malloc(n * sizeof(int));
```

Investigate whether AST analysis can preserve the source expression and its relationship to the declaration of `p`.

Distinguish this from knowing the runtime value of `n`.

The latter must come from actual runtime evidence.

### GCC compatibility

Investigate:

- GNU C extension support.
- GCC-specific predefined macros.
- Include paths.
- Compilation flags.
- Target ABI differences.
- Attribute handling.
- Inline assembly.
- Compiler-specific builtins.
- Parsing failures.

Determine what happens when Clang cannot correctly parse source accepted by GCC.

**AST enrichment must fail gracefully rather than invalidate a successful GCC execution trace.**

### Evaluate implementation options

Compare:

1. Clang AST dump or JSON output.
2. Clang tooling/libclang bindings.
3. Small source-pattern recognizers for specific missing facts.
4. No AST integration.

Consider:

- Startup overhead.
- Runtime overhead.
- Dependency size.
- Installation complexity.
- Compatibility.
- Extraction quality.
- Rust integration.
- Maintenance cost.

### Important

Clang AST must not become a second C execution interpreter.

It cannot fill missing runtime values, memory bytes, or actual pointer targets merely by inspecting syntax.

# 12. Investigate a Missing Metadata Registry

We are considering a lightweight mechanism to identify and potentially enrich missing metadata during Stage 1 trace construction.

Audit its feasibility.

Conceptual pipeline:

```text
GCC Compilation
       |
       v
DWARF Metadata Extraction
       |
       v
GDB Runtime Recording
       |
       v
Available Evidence + Missing Metadata Registry
       |
       v
Optional AST Enrichment
       |
       v
Finalized Execution Trace
```

### Investigate the registry design

Could missing information be recorded using lightweight references containing:

- Metadata category.
- Declaration or source identity.
- Source location.
- Related runtime observation reference.
- Reason information is missing.
- Possible enrichment source.
- Provenance of resolved metadata.
- Remaining uncertainty.

### Critical constraints

- Do not use memory addresses alone as declaration identities.
- Do not assume source line numbers uniquely identify expressions.
- Do not overwrite authoritative runtime observations with static guesses.
- Do not assume Clang's declaration and GCC's compiled declaration are automatically identical.
- Do not create large duplicated metadata records per checkpoint.
- Do not rerun AST analysis for every execution stop.

Evaluate whether missing static metadata should be enriched **before recording, during recording, or at finalization**.

Note that an enrichment system may need to collect static metadata before runtime recording even if the final trace is assembled afterward.

### Deliverable

Recommend the simplest reliable architecture for filling missing static metadata.

Do not implement the registry.

# 13. Audit the JSON schema

Inspect the complete current `DebugSessionTrace` structure and nested models.

Evaluate whether it can support richer metadata through additive fields.

### Examine

- `schema_version`.
- Optional field behavior.
- Serde defaults.

- Existing type representations.
- Variable metadata.
- Snapshot metadata.
- Heap event metadata.
- Disassembly records.
- Source references.
- Diagnostic evidence.
- Completeness metadata.

### Proposed design direction

Prefer:

- Optional fields for genuinely optional metadata.
- Shared static metadata tables when information repeats across checkpoints.
- Stable references from observations to metadata.
- Explicit unavailable statuses when needed.
- Provenance for metadata from different sources.

Avoid:

- Repeating complete struct layouts in every snapshot.
- Replacing the existing JSON format without necessity.
- Large redundant field collections.
- Invented defaults for unrecorded observations.
- Unnecessary schema migrations.

### Versioning investigation

Determine:

1. Which additive fields are safely backward-compatible.
2. Whether existing Serde readers accept unknown fields.
3. Whether new required fields would break old traces.
4. Whether existing schema version `2` can be preserved.
5. Which specific changes would actually require a new version.
6. What small compatibility changes TP-1/TP-2/TP-3 would need.

**Schema versioning must describe format compatibility, not whether execution completed or whether optional metadata is available.**

We are not requesting an elaborate versioning framework.

# 19. Classify every finding

For each identified limitation, assign exactly one primary category:

**A — Already available but underutilized**

The information exists in current traces or debug metadata but is not being used effectively.

**B — Existing machinery can be improved**

The information could be captured more reliably through changes to current GDB, MI2, memory-reading, or heap instrumentation logic.

**C — New DWARF extraction needed**

The metadata exists in compiled debug information but current Stage 1 cannot conveniently extract it.

**D — Optional AST enrichment useful**

Clang AST could provide additional static source information that DWARF does not reliably retain.

**E — Inherently uncertain or expensive**

Reliable recovery would require disproportionate instrumentation or information not available from our sources.

**F — Trace format or access limitation**

The evidence is present, but current serialization or parser interfaces do not preserve/expose it appropriately.

For every finding, include severity, evidence, proposed remedy, expected benefit, and cost.

# 20. Recommend implementation phases

Based on the findings, propose a concrete incremental implementation sequence.

The initial preference is:

**Part A — Optimize existing machinery**

1. GDB/MI2 command and checkpoint improvements.
2. Selective memory-byte and value capture improvements.
3. Heap instrumentation and event-attribution improvements.

**Part B — Add missing metadata sources**

4. `gimli` + `object` DWARF extraction.
5. Reliable correlation between static declarations and runtime observations.
6. Optional Clang AST enrichment and missing-metadata resolution.

**Part C — Integrate and validate**

7. JSON schema and Trace Parser adjustments.
8. Final regression, evidence-fidelity, and performance verification.

### Important

This order is provisional.

If the audit finds that DWARF extraction should precede particular GDB improvements, recommend changing the order.

If Clang AST is unnecessary, recommend omitting it.

If a proposed phase offers little benefit, recommend dropping it.

We want an efficient evidence pipeline, not additional components merely because they sound useful.

85:     pub signal: Option<String>,

14: /// Complete, configurable C build + link description.
15: ///
16: /// Engine-required flags (debug info, frame pointers, allocation wrapping)
17: /// are kept separate from user flags by the compiler module; user flags are
18: /// always passed through verbatim so they can override engine defaults when

20: #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, Default)]
21: #[serde(default)]
22: pub struct BuildConfig {
23:     /// Primary C source file (contains `main`).
24:     pub source_file: PathBuf,
25:     /// Additional C sources compiled and linked into the same binary.
26:     pub additional_sources: Vec<PathBuf>,
27:     /// Pre-built object files linked in without recompilation.
28:     pub object_files: Vec<PathBuf>,
29:     /// Include search directories (`-I`).
30:     pub include_dirs: Vec<PathBuf>,
31:     /// Preprocessor definitions (`-D`), given as `NAME` or `NAME=value`.
32:     pub defines: Vec<String>,
33:     /// Custom compiler flags, each element passed to gcc verbatim.
34:     pub compiler_flags: Vec<String>,
35:     /// Custom linker flags, each element passed to gcc verbatim.
36:     pub linker_flags: Vec<String>,
37:     /// Library search directories (`-L`).
38:     pub library_dirs: Vec<PathBuf>,
39:     /// Libraries to link (`-l`), without the leading `l`.
40:     pub libraries: Vec<String>,
41:     /// Optional executable name (defaults to a session-unique name).
42:     pub output_name: Option<String>,
43:     /// Working directory for compilation and (by default) execution.
44:     pub working_directory: Option<PathBuf>,
45: }

48:     /// All C sources that belong to the user's project (used to classify

1: //! Orchestrates the complete tracing pipeline.
2: //!
3: //! Pipeline:
4: //! 1. verify tools (gcc/gdb required; valgrind/addr2line optional)
5: //! 2. create a unique session temp directory; write the C runtime
6: //! 3. compile the debug binary (+ instrumentation) and the sanitized binary
7: //! 4. run GDB/MI2: breakpoint at `main`, step through user code, capture
8: //!    snapshots, ingest allocation events after every stop, read live heap
9: //!    contents through GDB within the configured budget
10: //! 5. resolve allocation caller locations with one batched `addr2line`
11: //! 6. on crash: run the sanitized binary as a separate diagnostic pass
12: //! 7. run Valgrind independently and correlate its findings with allocation
13: //!    ids
14: //! 8. assemble and return the structured [`DebugSessionTrace`]
15: //!
16: //! Partial results are always preserved: a timeout, a step limit or a crash
17: //! yields a trace containing everything captured up to that point.

51: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
52: async fn run_sanitizer_pass(
53:     asan_binary: &Path,
54:     program_args: &[String],
55:     working_directory: Option<&Path>,
56:     limits: &ExecutionLimits,
57:     crash: &mut Option<CrashReport>,
58:     started: Instant,

61:     notes: &mut Vec<String>,
62: ) -> Option<SanitizerReport> {

64:         trace.stage_results.sanitizer = skipped_stage(if crate::supervisor::cancelled() {
65:             "session interrupted"
66:         } else {
67:             "overall session deadline exhausted"
68:         });
69:         return None;
70:     }
71:     let mut report =
72:         sanitizer::run_sanitized(asan_binary, program_args, working_directory, limits).await;
73:     if report.reproduction == "reproduced"
74:         && !crash
75:             .as_ref()
76:             .is_some_and(|c| sanitizer::matches_crash(&report, c))
77:     {
78:         report.reproduction = "diagnostic_observed".into();
79:     }
80:     notes.push(format!("sanitizer pass: {}", report.reproduction));
81:     if report.reproduction == "reproduced" {
82:         let summary = report
83:             .message
84:             .clone()
85:             .or_else(|| report.error_category.clone())
86:             .filter(|s| !s.is_empty());
87:         if let Some(c) = crash.as_mut() {
88:             c.asan_summary = summary;
89:         }
90:     }
91:     trace.stage_results.sanitizer = crate::supervisor::stage(
92:         started,
93:         sanitizer_started,
94:         if report.cancelled {
95:             StageStatus::Cancelled
96:         } else if report.timed_out {
97:             StageStatus::TimedOut
98:         } else if report.reproduction == "inconclusive" || report.reproduction == "skipped" {
99:             StageStatus::Failed
100:         } else {
101:             StageStatus::Completed
102:         },
103:         report.exit_code,
104:         Some(report.reproduction.clone()),
105:         report.output_complete,
106:         report.sanitizer.is_some(),
107:     );
108:     Some(report)

585:     // ---- sanitizer / Valgrind stage ordering (V2.1, fixes F-02) --------------

1715:         }
1716:         // The finish chain resets once execution is back in user code.

1746:     }
1747:     // --- termination -----------------------------------------------------------
1748:     match result.status {
1749:         // Normal and crash endings: GDB shuts down gracefully.
1750:         ExecutionStatus::Completed | ExecutionStatus::Crashed => {
1751:             terminate(&mut session, cgroup.as_ref()).await;

1754:         ExecutionStatus::Timeout

1757:         | ExecutionStatus::ResourceLimitReached

1782:     if !matches!(

1810: enum SignalClass {
1811:     Fatal,
1812:     Resource,
1813:     Benign,
1814: }
1815: 
1816: fn classify_signal(name: Option<&str>) -> SignalClass {
1817:     match name {
1818:         Some(n) if FATAL_SIGNALS.contains(&n) => SignalClass::Fatal,
1819:         Some(n) if RESOURCE_SIGNALS.contains(&n) => SignalClass::Resource,
1820:         Some(n) if BENIGN_SIGNALS.contains(&n) => SignalClass::Benign,
1821:         // Unknown signal: conservatively fatal so we stop and report it.
1822:         _ => SignalClass::Fatal,
1823:     }
1824: }
1825: 
1826: fn observed_terminal(stop: &StoppedInfo) -> Option<ExecutionStatus> {
1827:     if stop.signal_name.as_deref() == Some("SIGKILL")
1828:         || stop.reason.as_deref() == Some("exited-signalled")
1829:     {
1830:         Some(ExecutionStatus::Interrupted)
1831:     } else if stop.is_signal() {
1832:         match classify_signal(stop.signal_name.as_deref()) {
1833:             SignalClass::Fatal => Some(ExecutionStatus::Crashed),
1834:             SignalClass::Resource => Some(ExecutionStatus::ResourceLimitReached),
1835:             SignalClass::Benign => None,
1836:         }
1837:     } else if stop.is_exit() {
1838:         Some(ExecutionStatus::Completed)
1839:     } else {
1840:         None
1841:     }
1842: }
1843: 
1844: fn remaining(deadline: Instant) -> Duration {
1845:     deadline.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now())
1846: }
1847: 
1848: fn step_timeout(wall_deadline: Instant) -> Duration {
1849:     remaining(wall_deadline).min(PER_STEP_TIMEOUT)
1850: }

1865: /// Debug aid: print the tail of GDB's raw MI stream (only when
1866: /// C_TRACE_DEBUG=1) so live protocol misbehaviour can be diagnosed.
1867: fn debug_dump_console(session: &GdbSession, why: &str) {
1868:     if !std::env::var_os("C_TRACE_DEBUG").is_some() {
1869:         return;
1870:     }
1871:     let log = session.console_log();
1872:     let mut tail_start = log.len().saturating_sub(6000);
1873:     while !log.is_char_boundary(tail_start) {
1874:         tail_start += 1;

2053: fn char_safe_head(s: &str, cap_bytes: usize) -> String {
2054:     if s.len() <= cap_bytes {
2055:         return s.to_string();

2057:     let mut cut = cap_bytes;
2058:     while !s.is_char_boundary(cut) {
2059:         cut -= 1;
2060:     }
2061:     s[..cut].to_string()
2062: }

2085: /// Inferior exit code: from the stop record, else from the
2086: /// `=thread-group-exited` notification in the backlog. MI emits the value as
2087: /// decimal in current versions but hex in some older ones; both accepted.
2088: fn exit_code_from(session: &mut GdbSession, stop: &StoppedInfo) -> Option<i32> {
2089:     if let Some(code) = &stop.exit_code {
2090:         return parse_mi_exit_code(code);
2091:     }
2092:     for record in session.take_backlog() {
2093:         if let crate::mi_parser::MiRecord::Notify { class, results } = &record {
2094:             if class == "thread-group-exited" {
2095:                 for r in results {
2096:                     if r.variable == "exit-code" {
2097:                         if let Some(v) = crate::mi_parser::as_const(&r.value) {
2098:                             if let Some(c) = parse_mi_exit_code(v) {
2099:                                 return Some(c);
2100:                             }
2101:                         }
2102:                     }
2103:                 }
2104:             }
2105:         }
2106:     }
2107:     None
2108: }
2109: 
2110: fn parse_mi_exit_code(text: &str) -> Option<i32> {
2111:     if let Some(hex) = text.strip_prefix("0x") {
2112:         return i32::from_str_radix(hex, 16).ok();
2113:     }
2114:     if text.starts_with('0') && text.len() > 1 {
2115:         return i32::from_str_radix(text, 8).ok();
2116:     }
2117:     if let Ok(v) = text.parse::<i32>() {
2118:         return Some(v);
2119:     }
2120:     u32::from_str_radix(text, 16).ok().map(|v| v as i32)
2121: }

2153:                 block.allocation_line = state.caller_line;
2154:                 block.realloc_from_id = state
2155:                     .realloc_from_id
2156:                     .map(|id| timeline.global_id(parent_pid, id));
2157:                 block.allocation_id = timeline.global_id(parent_pid, block.allocation_id);

2159:         }
2160:     }
2161:     snapshots

2169:         .map(|e| {

2180: /// Final heap state: every reconstructed block with its end-of-run status.
2181: /// `raw_bytes_hex` carries the last bytes captured while the block was alive
2182: /// (from any snapshot); freed blocks keep that historical capture, live
2183: /// blocks the most recent one.
2184: fn build_heap_state(
2185:     timeline: &HeapTimeline,
2186:     snapshots: &[ExecutionSnapshot],
2187:     _parent_pid: Option<u32>,
2188: ) -> Vec<HeapBlockInfo> {
2189:     let mut last_contents: HashMap<u64, (String, Option<u64>)> = HashMap::new();
2190:     for snap in snapshots {
2191:         for b in &snap.heap_blocks {
2192:             if let Some(hex) = &b.raw_bytes_hex {
2193:                 last_contents.insert(b.allocation_id, (hex.clone(), b.observed_at_stop));
2194:             }
2195:         }
2196:     }
2197:     timeline
2198:         .blocks()
2199:         .iter()
2200:         .map(|b| {
2201:             let global = timeline.global_id(b.pid, b.allocation_id);
2202:             HeapBlockInfo {
2203:                 observed_at_stop: last_contents.get(&global).and_then(|(_, stop)| *stop),
2204:                 allocation_id: global,
2205:                 address: format!("0x{:x}", b.addr),
2206:                 size_bytes: b.size,
2207:                 allocation_type: b.alloc_type.to_string(),
2208:                 is_freed: b.freed,
2209:                 allocation_file: b.caller_file.clone(),
2210:                 allocation_line: b.caller_line,

2212:                 memory_read_error: None,
2213:                 realloc_from_id: b.realloc_from_id.map(|id| timeline.global_id(b.pid, id)),
2214:             }

99: /// Verify that a tool exists and can be executed; returns its version line.
100: pub async fn probe_tool(tool: &str, version_arg: &str) -> Result<String> {
101:     let tool_owned = tool.to_string();
102:     let version_arg = version_arg.to_string();
103:     let version_display = version_arg.clone();
104:     let output = crate::supervisor::output(
105:         Command::new(&tool_owned).arg(version_arg),
106:         crate::supervisor::stage_deadline(3),
107:         1024 * 1024,
108:     )
109:     .await
110:     .map_err(|e| match e {
111:         EngineError::Cancelled => EngineError::Cancelled,
112:         _ => EngineError::MissingTool {
113:             tool: tool_owned.clone(),
114:             reason: format!("could not spawn `{}`: {}", tool_owned, e),
115:         },
116:     })?;
117:     if output.cancelled {
118:         return Err(EngineError::Cancelled);
119:     }
120:     if !output.status.is_some_and(|s| s.success()) {
121:         return Err(EngineError::MissingTool {
122:             tool: tool_owned.clone(),
123:             reason: format!("`{} {}` failed", tool_owned, version_display),
124:         });
125:     }
126:     let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
127:     Ok(text.lines().next().unwrap_or_default().to_string())
128: }

132: pub async fn detect_diagnostics_format(cc: &str) -> DiagnosticsFormat {
133:     for (fmt, flag) in [

143:             1024 * 1024,

150:                     continue; // flag unsupported, try next
151:                 }
152:                 return fmt;
153:             }
154:             Err(_) => continue,

199: fn diag_from_gcc_json(d: &GccJsonDiagnostic) -> CompilerDiagnostic {
200:     let (file, line, column) = d
201:         .locations
202:         .first()
203:         .map(|l| l.caret.as_deref().unwrap_or(l))
204:         .map(|l| {
205:             (
206:                 l.file
207:                     .as_ref()
208:                     .and_then(|f| f.name())
209:                     .unwrap_or_else(|| "<unknown>".into()),
210:                 l.line
211:                     .as_ref()
212:                     .and_then(|n| n.as_u64())
213:                     .unwrap_or(0)
214:                     .min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32,
215:                 l.column
216:                     .as_ref()
217:                     .and_then(|n| n.as_u64())
218:                     .unwrap_or(0)
219:                     .min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32,
220:             )
221:         })
222:         .unwrap_or(("<unknown>".into(), 0, 0));
223:     CompilerDiagnostic {
224:         file,
225:         line,
226:         column,
227:         kind: d.kind.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "message".into()),
228:         message: d.message.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
229:     }
230: }

232: fn parse_legacy_gcc_json(stderr: &str) -> Option<Vec<CompilerDiagnostic>> {
233:     let trimmed = stderr.trim();
234:     if !trimmed.starts_with('[') {
235:         return None;
236:     }
237:     // GCC prints one JSON document per translation unit; parse the stream of
238:     // consecutive documents.
239:     let stream = serde_json::Deserializer::from_str(trimmed).into_iter::<Vec<GccJsonDiagnostic>>();
240:     let mut out = Vec::new();
241:     let mut any = false;
242:     for doc in stream {
243:         let diags = doc.ok()?;
244:         any = true;
245:         for d in diags {
246:             out.push(diag_from_gcc_json(&d));
247:             // GCC attaches notes as `children`; flatten them so the IDE can
248:             // show them as separate entries.
249:             for child in &d.children {
250:                 let mut c = diag_from_gcc_json(child);
251:                 if c.kind.is_empty() {
252:                     c.kind = "note".into();
253:                 }
254:                 out.push(c);
255:             }
256:         }
257:     }
258:     any.then_some(out)
259: }

317: fn parse_sarif(stderr: &str) -> Option<Vec<CompilerDiagnostic>> {
318:     let trimmed = stderr.trim();
319:     if !trimmed.starts_with('{') {
320:         return None;
321:     }
322:     // GCC prints one SARIF document per translation unit (even when a unit
323:     // has no diagnostics); parse the stream of consecutive documents.
324:     let stream = serde_json::Deserializer::from_str(trimmed).into_iter::<SarifDoc>();
325:     let mut out = Vec::new();
326:     let mut any = false;
327:     for doc in stream {
328:         let doc = doc.ok()?;
329:         any = true;
330:         for run in doc.runs {
331:             for r in run.results {
332:                 let (file, line, column) = r
333:                     .locations
334:                     .first()
335:                     .and_then(|l| l.physical_location.as_ref())
336:                     .map(|p| {
337:                         (
338:                             p.artifact_location
339:                                 .as_ref()
340:                                 .and_then(|a| a.uri.clone())
341:                                 .unwrap_or_else(|| "<unknown>".into()),
342:                             p.region
343:                                 .as_ref()
344:                                 .and_then(|rg| rg.startline.as_ref().and_then(|n| n.as_u64()))
345:                                 .unwrap_or(0)
346:                                 .min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32,
347:                             p.region
348:                                 .as_ref()
349:                                 .and_then(|rg| rg.startcolumn.as_ref().and_then(|n| n.as_u64()))
350:                                 .unwrap_or(0)
351:                                 .min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32,
352:                         )
353:                     })
354:                     .unwrap_or(("<unknown>".into(), 0, 0));
355:                 out.push(CompilerDiagnostic {
356:                     file,
357:                     line,
358:                     column,
359:                     kind: r.level.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "message".into()),
360:                     message: r.message.and_then(|m| m.text).unwrap_or_default(),
361:                 });
362:             }
363:         }
364:     }
365:     any.then_some(out)
366: }

368: /// Build a fallback diagnostic from plain-text stderr (e.g. linker errors).
369: fn text_diagnostics(stderr: &str) -> Vec<CompilerDiagnostic> {
370:     let trimmed = stderr.trim();
371:     if trimmed.is_empty() {
372:         return Vec::new();
373:     }
374:     let kind = if trimmed.contains("undefined reference")
375:         || trimmed.contains("multiple definition")
376:         || trimmed.contains("ld returned")
377:     {
378:         "linker-error"
379:     } else {
380:         "error"
381:     };
382:     let message: String = trimmed.chars().take(4000).collect();
383:     vec![CompilerDiagnostic {
384:         file: String::new(),
385:         line: 0,
386:         column: 0,
387:         kind: kind.into(),
388:         message,
389:     }]
390: }

392: /// Build the full gcc argument vector for one binary.
393: fn build_argv(build: &BuildConfig, opts: &CompileOptions, diag_flag: Option<&str>) -> Vec<String> {
394:     let mut argv: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
395: 
396:     // --- engine-required flags (kept separate from user flags) ---
397:     argv.push("-g".into());
398:     argv.push("-O0".into());
399:     argv.push("-fno-omit-frame-pointer".into());
400:     if opts.sanitized {
401:         argv.push(format!("-fsanitize={}", opts.sanitizer_variant));
402:     }
403:     if let Some(flag) = diag_flag {
404:         argv.push(flag.into());
405:     }
406:     if opts.include_alloc_tracker {
407:         argv.extend(
408:             [
409:                 "-Wl,--wrap=malloc",
410:                 "-Wl,--wrap=calloc",
411:                 "-Wl,--wrap=realloc",
412:                 "-Wl,--wrap=free",
413:             ]
414:             .iter()
415:             .map(|s| s.to_string()),
416:         );
417:     }
418: 
419:     // --- user configuration ---
420:     for d in &build.defines {
421:         argv.push(format!("-D{}", d));
422:     }
423:     for dir in &build.include_dirs {
424:         argv.push(format!("-I{}", dir.display()));
425:     }
426:     argv.extend(build.compiler_flags.iter().cloned());
427: 
428:     // --- inputs ---
429:     argv.push(build.source_file.display().to_string());
430:     for s in &build.additional_sources {
431:         argv.push(s.display().to_string());
432:     }
433:     if let Some(tracker) = &opts.tracker_source {
434:         argv.push(tracker.display().to_string());
435:     }
436:     for o in &build.object_files {
437:         argv.push(o.display().to_string());
438:     }
439: 
440:     // --- linking ---
441:     for dir in &build.library_dirs {
442:         argv.push(format!("-L{}", dir.display()));
443:     }
444:     argv.extend(build.linker_flags.iter().cloned());
445:     for lib in &build.libraries {
446:         argv.push(format!("-l{}", lib));
447:     }
448: 
449:     argv.push("-o".into());
450:     argv.push(opts.output_path.display().to_string());
451:     argv
452: }

454: /// Compile (and link) the configured project once.
455: pub async fn compile(
456:     build: &BuildConfig,
457:     cc: &str,
458:     opts: &CompileOptions,
459:     format: DiagnosticsFormat,
460: ) -> Result<CompilationOutput> {
461:     if build.source_file.as_os_str().is_empty() {
462:         return Err(EngineError::Config("no source file configured".into()));
463:     }
464:     let diag_flag = match format {
465:         DiagnosticsFormat::LegacyJson => Some("-fdiagnostics-format=json"),
466:         DiagnosticsFormat::Sarif => Some("-fdiagnostics-format=sarif-stderr"),
467:         DiagnosticsFormat::Text => None,
468:     };
469:     let argv = build_argv(build, opts, diag_flag);
470: 
471:     let mut cmd = Command::new(cc);
472:     cmd.args(&argv);
473:     if let Some(dir) = &build.working_directory {
474:         cmd.current_dir(dir);
475:     }
476:     // Compilation gets its own generous ceiling; the execution limits apply
477:     // to the inferior, not to the compiler.
478:     let output =
479:         crate::supervisor::output(&mut cmd, crate::supervisor::deadline(), 8 * 1024 * 1024).await?;
480:     if output.timed_out {
481:         return Err(crate::supervisor::timeout_error("compilation"));
482:     }
483:     if output.cancelled {
484:         return Err(EngineError::Cancelled);
485:     }
486: 
487:     let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).into_owned();
488:     let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).into_owned();
489:     let _ = stdout; // gcc diagnostics go to stderr
490: 
491:     let success = output.status.is_some_and(|s| s.success());
492: 
493:     let diagnostics = match format {
494:         DiagnosticsFormat::LegacyJson => {
495:             parse_legacy_gcc_json(&stderr).unwrap_or_else(|| text_diagnostics(&stderr))
496:         }
497:         DiagnosticsFormat::Sarif => {
498:             parse_sarif(&stderr).unwrap_or_else(|| text_diagnostics(&stderr))
499:         }
500:         DiagnosticsFormat::Text => {
501:             // Text mode: only produce a diagnostic when the build failed or
502:             // stderr is non-empty (warnings are unparseable in text mode but
503:             // must not be lost).
504:             if success && stderr.trim().is_empty() {
505:                 Vec::new()
506:             } else {
507:                 text_diagnostics(&stderr)
508:             }
509:         }
510:     };
511:     // In JSON modes gcc prints only the diagnostic JSON; if the toolchain
512:     // succeeded but no diagnostics came back, that is normal (no warnings).
513:     let has_errors = diagnostics
514:         .iter()
515:         .any(|d| d.kind == "error" || d.kind == "linker-error" || d.kind == "fatal error");
516:     let success = success && !has_errors;
517: 
518:     Ok(CompilationOutput {
519:         sanitizer_variant: opts.sanitized.then(|| opts.sanitizer_variant.to_string()),
520:         success,
521:         exit_code: output.status.and_then(|s| s.code()).unwrap_or(-1),
522:         binary_path: opts.output_path.clone(),
523:         diagnostics,
524:         raw_stderr: stderr,
525:         diagnostics_format: format,
526:     })
527: }
528: 
529: /// Convenience: compile with the standard engine layout for one session dir.
530: pub async fn compile_project(
531:     build: &BuildConfig,
532:     session_dir: &Path,
533:     tracker_source: Option<PathBuf>,
534: ) -> Result<(CompilationOutput, CompilationOutput)> {
535:     let cc = "gcc";
536:     let _gcc_version = probe_tool(cc, "--version").await?;
537:     let format = detect_diagnostics_format(cc).await;
538: 
539:     let debug_name = build
540:         .output_name
541:         .clone()
542:         .unwrap_or_else(|| "program".to_string());
543:     let debug_out = session_dir.join(format!("{}_debug", debug_name));
544: 
545:     let debug_opts = CompileOptions::debug(debug_out, tracker_source);
546:     let debug_result = compile(build, cc, &debug_opts, format).await?;
547: 
548:     if !debug_result.success {
549:         return Ok((debug_result, not_built()));
550:     }
551: 
552:     // The sanitized build reuses the user's configuration but not the
553:     // instrumentation runtime: ASan replaces the allocator at interception
554:     // level, and wrapping the allocator underneath ASan would double-report.
555:     // Sanitizer runtimes may be partially installed (e.g. libasan present but
556:     // libubsan missing), so degrade: combined → asan-only → ubsan-only → none.
557:     let asan_out = session_dir.join(format!("{}_asan", debug_name));
558:     let variants: [(&'static str, &'static str); 3] = [
559:         ("address,undefined", "asan+ubsan"),
560:         ("address", "asan"),
561:         ("undefined", "ubsan"),
562:     ];
563:     let mut asan_result = not_built();
564:     for (flag, _label) in variants {
565:         let opts = CompileOptions::sanitized_with_variant(asan_out.clone(), flag);
566:         let r = match compile(build, cc, &opts, format).await {
567:             Ok(result) => result,
568:             Err(e) => {
569:                 // The already completed debug build must survive a failed optional build.
570:                 asan_result.raw_stderr = e.to_string();
571:                 break;
572:             }
573:         };
574:         if r.success {
575:             asan_result = r;
576:             break;
577:         }
578:     }
579: 
580:     Ok((debug_result, asan_result))
581: }
582: 
583: fn not_built() -> CompilationOutput {
584:     CompilationOutput {
585:         sanitizer_variant: None,
586:         success: false,
587:         exit_code: -1,
588:         binary_path: PathBuf::new(),
589:         diagnostics: Vec::new(),
590:         raw_stderr: String::new(),
591:         diagnostics_format: DiagnosticsFormat::Text,
592:     }
593: }
594:

600:         let diagnostics = parse_legacy_gcc_json(r#"[{"kind":"error","message":"native error","locations":[{"caret":{"file":"input.c","line":7,"column":3}}]}] []"#).unwrap();

1: //! Custom C allocation instrumentation runtime and Rust-side event
2: //! processing.
3: //!
4: //! The C runtime (`c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c`, embedded with `include_str!`)
5: //! is linked into the debug binary with `-Wl,--wrap=malloc|calloc|realloc|free`
6: //! and appends one event line per allocation operation to a dedicated file.
7: //! This module:
8: //!
9: //! * tails that file incrementally (the inferior is *stopped* whenever we
10: //!   read, so the file content is exactly the event history up to the
11: //!   current stop),
12: //! * parses the event format into [`RawEvent`]s,
13: //! * reconstructs the chronological heap timeline: live blocks, freed
14: //!   blocks, lifetimes, realloc chains, per-event heap usage,
15: //! * resolves caller return addresses to `file:line` with a single batched
16: //!   `addr2line` invocation at the end of the run.
17: //!
18: //! Allocation ids are per-process counters; `(pid, id)` is the unique key
19: //! internally. When more than one pid appears (forked children), serialized
20: //! ids are widened to `(pid << 32) | id` at finalization so the trace never
21: //! contains a duplicate id (see `HeapTimeline::finalize`).

81: /// Parse one event line
82: /// (`pid seq kind id addr size old_id old_addr caller status`).
83: pub fn parse_event_line(line: &str) -> Result<RawEvent> {
84:     let fields: Vec<&str> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
85:     if fields.len() != 10 {
86:         return Err(crate::error::EngineError::AllocationEventParse {
87:             line: 0,
88:             message: format!("expected 10 fields, found {}", fields.len()),
89:         });
90:     }
91:     let num = |i: usize| -> Result<u64> {
92:         fields[i]
93:             .parse::<u64>()
94:             .map_err(|_| crate::error::EngineError::AllocationEventParse {
95:                 line: 0,
96:                 message: format!("invalid decimal field {}: {:?}", i, fields[i]),
97:             })
98:     };
99:     let hex = |i: usize| -> Result<u64> {
100:         u64::from_str_radix(fields[i], 16).map_err(|_| {
101:             crate::error::EngineError::AllocationEventParse {
102:                 line: 0,
103:                 message: format!("invalid hex field {}: {:?}", i, fields[i]),
104:             }
105:         })
106:     };
107:     let kind = match fields[2] {
108:         "malloc" => RawKind::Malloc,
109:         "calloc" => RawKind::Calloc,
110:         "realloc" => RawKind::Realloc,
111:         "free" => RawKind::Free,
112:         other => {
113:             return Err(crate::error::EngineError::AllocationEventParse {
114:                 line: 0,
115:                 message: format!("unknown kind {other:?}"),
116:             })
117:         }
118:     };
119:     let status = match fields[9] {
120:         "ok" => RawStatus::Ok,
121:         "failed" => RawStatus::Failed,
122:         "overflow" => RawStatus::Overflow,
123:         "ok_same" => RawStatus::OkSame,
124:         "ok_moved" => RawStatus::OkMoved,
125:         "new" => RawStatus::New,
126:         "zero" => RawStatus::Zero,
127:         "null" => RawStatus::Null,
128:         "unknown" => RawStatus::Unknown,
129:         other => {
130:             return Err(crate::error::EngineError::AllocationEventParse {
131:                 line: 0,
132:                 message: format!("unknown status {other:?}"),
133:             })
134:         }
135:     };
136:     Ok(RawEvent {
137:         pid: num(0)?.min(u32::MAX as u64) as u32,
138:         seq: num(1)?,
139:         kind,
140:         id: num(3)?,
141:         addr: hex(4)?,
142:         size: num(5)?,
143:         old_id: num(6)?,
144:         old_addr: hex(7)?,
145:         caller: hex(8)?,
146:         status,
147:     })

150: /// Incremental reader for the event trace file.
151: pub struct EventFileReader {
152:     path: PathBuf,
153:     offset: u64,
154:     partial: Vec<u8>,
155:     pub parse_errors: Vec<String>,
156: }
157: 
158: impl EventFileReader {
159:     pub fn new(path: PathBuf) -> Self {
160:         Self {
161:             path,
162:             offset: 0,
163:             partial: Vec::new(),
164:             parse_errors: Vec::new(),
165:         }
166:     }
167: 
168:     /// Read and parse all events appended since the last call. Partial
169:     /// trailing lines (crash mid-write) are buffered until complete.
170:     pub fn read_new(&mut self) -> Vec<RawEvent> {
171:         let mut events = Vec::new();
172:         let file = match File::open(&self.path) {
173:             Ok(f) => f,
174:             Err(_) => return events, // not created yet: inferior not started
175:         };
176:         let mut reader = BufReader::new(file);
177:         if reader.seek(SeekFrom::Start(self.offset)).is_err() {
178:             return events;
179:         }
180:         let mut buffer = Vec::new();
181:         // The event file is bounded by the program's allocation count and
182:         // the engine's caps; read everything appended since last time.
183:         if reader.read_to_end(&mut buffer).is_err() {
184:             return events;
185:         }
186: 
187:         let mut data = std::mem::take(&mut self.partial);
188:         data.extend_from_slice(&buffer);
189:         let mut consumed = 0usize;
190:         let mut pos = 0usize;
191:         while pos < data.len() {
192:             match data[pos..].iter().position(|&b| b == b'\n') {
193:                 Some(nl) => {
194:                     let line = &data[pos..pos + nl];
195:                     consumed = pos + nl + 1;
196:                     pos += nl + 1;
197:                     if line.is_empty() {
198:                         continue;
199:                     }
200:                     match parse_event_line(&String::from_utf8_lossy(line)) {
201:                         Ok(ev) => events.push(ev),
202:                         Err(e) => {
203:                             if self.parse_errors.len() < 50 {
204:                                 self.parse_errors.push(e.to_string());
205:                             }
206:                         }
207:                     }
208:                 }
209:                 None => break, // incomplete line, keep for next call
210:             }
211:         }
212:         // Keep the unconsumed partial tail in memory; the file offset always
213:         // points past the bytes we have already READ (not parsed), so the
214:         // buffered partial is never re-read from disk.
215:         self.partial = data[consumed..].to_vec();
216:         self.offset += buffer.len() as u64;
217:         events
218:     }
219: }

287:     /// Ingest one raw event, updating block state and event history.
288:     pub fn ingest(&mut self, ev: &RawEvent) {

290:         let addr_key = (ev.pid, ev.addr);
291:         let mut detail: Option<String> = None;
292: 
293:         match (ev.kind, ev.status) {
294:             (RawKind::Calloc, RawStatus::Overflow) => {
295:                 self.push_event(
296:                     HeapEventType::AllocationFailed,
297:                     ev,
298:                     Some(
299:                         "calloc size product overflow; requested byte size is not representable"
300:                             .into(),
301:                     ),
302:                 );
303:             }
304:             (RawKind::Malloc, RawStatus::Ok) | (RawKind::Calloc, RawStatus::Ok) => {
305:                 self.add_block(
306:                     ev,
307:                     if ev.kind == RawKind::Malloc {
308:                         "malloc"
309:                     } else {
310:                         "calloc"
311:                     },
312:                     None,
313:                 );
314:                 self.push_event(HeapEventType::Allocated, ev, detail);
315:             }
316:             (RawKind::Malloc, RawStatus::Failed) | (RawKind::Calloc, RawStatus::Failed) => {
317:                 detail = Some(
318:                     if ev.size == 0 {
319:                         "zero-size allocation returned NULL; no allocation observed"
320:                     } else {
321:                         "allocation failed (out of memory or invalid request)"
322:                     }
323:                     .into(),
324:                 );
325:                 self.push_event(HeapEventType::AllocationFailed, ev, detail);
326:             }
327:             (RawKind::Realloc, RawStatus::New) => {
328:                 self.add_block(ev, "realloc", None);
329:                 self.push_event(HeapEventType::Reallocated, ev, None);
330:             }
331:             (RawKind::Realloc, RawStatus::OkSame) => {
332:                 if let Some(&idx) = self.alive_by_key.get(&key) {
333:                     let old_size = self.blocks[idx].size;
334:                     self.blocks[idx].size = ev.size;
335:                     let usage = self.live_bytes.entry(ev.pid).or_insert(0);
336:                     *usage = usage.saturating_sub(old_size).saturating_add(ev.size);
337:                 }
338:                 self.push_event(HeapEventType::Reallocated, ev, None);
339:             }
340:             (RawKind::Realloc, RawStatus::OkMoved) => {
341:                 // Retire the old block; the new block keeps a link to it.

345:                         self.blocks[old_idx].free_seq = ev.seq;

350:                     }
351:                 }
352:                 self.add_block(ev, "realloc", Some(ev.old_id));
353:                 self.push_event(HeapEventType::Reallocated, ev, None);

355:             (RawKind::Realloc, RawStatus::Zero) => {
356:                 // glibc: realloc(p, 0) frees p and returns NULL.

359:                     self.blocks[old_idx].free_seq = ev.seq;
360:                     self.alive_by_key.remove(&(ev.pid, ev.old_id));
361:                     self.alive_by_addr.remove(&(ev.pid, ev.old_addr));
362:                     let usage = self.live_bytes.entry(ev.pid).or_insert(0);
363:                     *usage = usage.saturating_sub(self.blocks[old_idx].size);
364:                 }
365:                 detail = Some("realloc(ptr, 0): glibc freed the block and returned NULL".into());
366:                 self.push_event(HeapEventType::Reallocated, ev, detail);

368:             (RawKind::Realloc, RawStatus::Failed) => {
369:                 // Failure preserves the original allocation — never treat

371:                 detail = Some(

374:                     } else {
375:                         "realloc failed: original allocation preserved"
376:                     }
377:                     .into(),
378:                 );
379:                 self.push_event(HeapEventType::AllocationFailed, ev, detail);
380:             }
381:             (RawKind::Free, RawStatus::Ok) => {
382:                 if let Some(&idx) = self.alive_by_key.get(&key) {
383:                     self.blocks[idx].freed = true;

386:                     self.alive_by_addr.remove(&addr_key);
387:                     let usage = self.live_bytes.entry(ev.pid).or_insert(0);
388:                     *usage = usage.saturating_sub(self.blocks[idx].size);

390:                 self.push_event(HeapEventType::Freed, ev, None);
391:             }
392:             (RawKind::Free, RawStatus::Null) => {
393:                 detail = Some("free(NULL) is a no-op".into());

399:                 if let Some(&idx) = self.alive_by_addr.get(&addr_key) {

403:                     self.alive_by_key.remove(&(ev.pid, id));
404:                     self.alive_by_addr.remove(&addr_key);

427:                     ev,
428:                     Some("unexpected event status".into()),

431:         }
432:     }

434:     fn add_block(&mut self, ev: &RawEvent, alloc_type: &'static str, realloc_from: Option<u64>) {
435:         if self.blocks.len() >= self.max_blocks {

437:             return;
438:         }
439:         let idx = self.blocks.len();
440:         self.blocks.push(BlockState {
441:             pid: ev.pid,
442:             allocation_id: ev.id,
443:             addr: ev.addr,
444:             size: ev.size,
445:             alloc_type,

541: /// Resolved caller location: function, file, line.
542: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
543: pub struct CallerInfo {
544:     pub func: String,
545:     pub file: String,
546:     pub line: u32,
547: }
548: 
549: /// Resolve caller return addresses to `file:line` using ONE batched
550: /// `addr2line -f -C -e <binary>` invocation.
551: ///
552: /// addr2line prints two lines per requested address: the function name and
553: /// the `file:line` pair. Addresses that cannot be resolved (no debug info,
554: /// foreign module) yield "??"/"?:0" and are absent from the returned map.
555: pub async fn resolve_caller_locations(
556:     binary: &Path,
557:     callers: &[u64],
558: ) -> Result<HashMap<u64, CallerInfo>> {
559:     let mut unique: Vec<u64> = callers.to_vec();
560:     unique.sort_unstable();
561:     unique.dedup();
562:     let mut out = HashMap::new();
563:     for chunk in unique.chunks(512) {
564:         let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new("addr2line");
565:         cmd.args(["-f", "-C", "-e"])
566:             .arg(binary)
567:             .args(chunk.iter().map(|pc| format!("0x{pc:x}")));
568:         let output =
569:             crate::supervisor::output(&mut cmd, crate::supervisor::stage_deadline(3), 1024 * 1024)
570:                 .await?;
571:         if output.timed_out || !output.status.is_some_and(|s| s.success()) {
572:             return Err(EngineError::Other("addr2line failed or timed out".into()));
573:         }
574:         let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
575:         let lines: Vec<String> = text.lines().map(str::to_owned).collect();
576:         // Group pairwise: (func, "file:line") for each requested address.
577:         for (i, pc) in chunk.iter().enumerate() {
578:             let func_line = lines.get(i * 2).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
579:             let loc_line = lines.get(i * 2 + 1).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
580:             let (file, line_no) = split_addr2line_location(&loc_line);
581:             if file.is_empty() || line_no == 0 {
582:                 continue;
583:             }
584:             out.insert(
585:                 *pc,
586:                 CallerInfo {
587:                     func: if func_line == "??" {
588:                         String::new()
589:                     } else {
590:                         func_line
591:                     },
592:                     file,
593:                     line: line_no,
594:                 },
595:             );
596:         }
597:     }
598:     Ok(out)
599: }

601: /// Split "path/to/file.c:42" (or "file.c:42", "?:0", "file.c:?").
602: fn split_addr2line_location(loc: &str) -> (String, u32) {
603:     let loc = loc.trim();
604:     if loc.is_empty() || loc == "??:0" || loc == "?:0" {
605:         return (String::new(), 0);
606:     }
607:     match loc.rfind(':') {
608:         Some(pos) => {
609:             let file = loc[..pos].to_string();
610:             let line = loc[pos + 1..].trim().parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(0);
611:             (file, line)
612:         }
613:         None => (String::new(), 0),
614:     }
615: }
