1: /*
2:  * c-trace-engine allocation instrumentation runtime.
3:  *
4:  * Linked into the debug binary via `-Wl,--wrap=malloc|calloc|realloc|free`.
5:  * Every allocation event is appended, with a single unbuffered write(), to a
6:  * dedicated trace file named by the C_TRACE_EVENT_FILE environment variable
7:  * (never to the program's stdout/stderr).
8:  *
9:  * Event line format (space-separated, one event per line):
10:  *
11:  *     pid seq kind id addr size old_id old_addr caller status
12:  *
13:  *   pid      OS pid of the recording process (distinguishes forked children)
14:  *   seq      per-process event sequence number (1-based, monotonic)
15:  *   kind     "malloc" | "calloc" | "realloc" | "free"
16:  *   id       allocation id (per-process counter; stable for the block's
17:  *            lifetime; 0 when there is no tracked allocation)
18:  *   addr     returned address, hexadecimal (0 on failure)
19:  *   size     requested size in bytes (calloc: nmemb*size)
20:  *   old_id   previous allocation id for realloc (0 otherwise)
21:  *   old_addr previous address for realloc (0 otherwise)
22:  *   caller   return address of the caller (resolved later via addr2line)
23:  *   status   ok | failed | ok_same | ok_moved | new | zero | null | unknown
24:  *
25:  * Constraints honored by this runtime:
26:  *   - No dynamic allocation inside the tracking path: fixed-size table,
27:  *     stack buffers, snprintf + write() only.
28:  *   - A __thread recursion guard makes any allocation triggered *by the
29:  *     tracker itself* pass through unrecorded.
30:  *   - A single spinlock (no futexes, no allocation) serializes table and
31:  *     sequence updates; program semantics are unchanged: every wrapper calls
32:  *     the real allocator exactly once and returns its result verbatim.
33:  *   - Failed allocations never modify tracked state: a failed realloc keeps
34:  *     the original block alive and marked as such.
35:  *   - The table maps address -> {id,size}; it is keyed per-process and the
36:  *     Rust side additionally matches by address, so even a table overflow
37:  *     (tracked blocks beyond CTE_TABLE_SLOTS) stays reconstructable.
38:  *
39:  * Known limitations (documented in README):
40:  *   - --wrap only intercepts references from objects linked into the binary.
41:  *     Allocations made internally by shared libraries (glibc internals,
42:  *     dlsym-loaded allocators, strdup's internal allocation) are NOT wrapped.
43:  *   - __builtin_return_address(0) can be unreliable for tail-calls or fully
44:  *     inlined callers; -O0 keeps this rare.
45:  *   - If the environment variable is unset the runtime is fully passive.
46:  */
47: 
48: #define _GNU_SOURCE
49: #include <stdio.h>
50: #include <stdlib.h>
51: #include <string.h>
52: #include <stdint.h>
53: #include <limits.h>
54: #if ULONG_MAX != UINT64_MAX
55: #error "c-trace allocation runtime requires a 64-bit unsigned long target"
56: #endif
57: #include <unistd.h>
58: #include <fcntl.h>
59: #include <errno.h>
60: 
61: /* 2^17 slots ≈ 131k concurrently tracked live addresses (3 MiB static). */
62: #define CTE_TABLE_SLOTS (1u << 17)
63: #define CTE_TABLE_MASK (CTE_TABLE_SLOTS - 1u)
64: 
65: typedef struct {
66:     unsigned long addr; /* 0 = empty slot */
67:     unsigned long id;
68:     unsigned long size;
69: } cte_slot;
70: 
71: static cte_slot g_table[CTE_TABLE_SLOTS];
72: static int g_fd = -1;
73: static volatile int g_spin = 0;
74: static unsigned long g_seq; /* last issued event sequence */
75: static unsigned long g_ids; /* last issued allocation id */
76: static __thread int g_busy = 0;
77: 
78: extern void *__real_malloc(size_t);
79: extern void *__real_calloc(size_t, size_t);
80: extern void *__real_realloc(void *, size_t);
81: extern void __real_free(void *);
82: 
83: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
84: /* Minimal synchronization: test-and-set spinlock, no allocation.      */
85: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
86: 
87: static void cte_lock(void)
88: {
89:     for (;;) {
90:         if (__sync_bool_compare_and_swap(&g_spin, 0, 1))
91:             return;
92:         while (g_spin) {
93:             /* spin */
94:         }
95:     }
96: }
97: 
98: static void cte_unlock(void)
99: {
100:     __sync_lock_release(&g_spin);
101: }
102: 
103: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
104: /* Fixed-size open-addressing table: address -> {id, size}.            */
105: /* Linear probing with standard back-shift deletion (no tombstones).   */
106: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
107: 
108: static unsigned long cte_hash(unsigned long x)
109: {
110:     x ^= x >> 33;
111:     x *= 0xff51afd7ed558ccdUL;
112:     x ^= x >> 33;
113:     x *= 0xc4ceb9fe1a85ec53UL;
114:     x ^= x >> 33;
115:     return x;
116: }
117: 
118: static cte_slot *cte_find(unsigned long addr)
119: {
120:     unsigned long i = cte_hash(addr) & CTE_TABLE_MASK;
121:     for (unsigned long n = 0; n < CTE_TABLE_SLOTS; n++, i = (i + 1) & CTE_TABLE_MASK) {
122:         if (g_table[i].addr == 0)
123:             return NULL; /* hit an empty slot: not present */
124:         if (g_table[i].addr == addr)
125:             return &g_table[i];
126:     }
127:     return NULL;
128: }
129: 
130: static int cte_insert(unsigned long addr, unsigned long id, unsigned long size)
131: {
132:     unsigned long i = cte_hash(addr) & CTE_TABLE_MASK;
133:     for (unsigned long n = 0; n < CTE_TABLE_SLOTS; n++, i = (i + 1) & CTE_TABLE_MASK) {
134:         if (g_table[i].addr == 0) {
135:             g_table[i].addr = addr;
136:             g_table[i].id = id;
137:             g_table[i].size = size;
138:             return 1;
139:         }
140:     }
141:     return 0; /* table full: events still recorded, id resolution falls
142:                  back to the Rust-side address map */
143: }
144: 
145: static void cte_remove(unsigned long addr)
146: {
147:     unsigned long i = cte_hash(addr) & CTE_TABLE_MASK;
148:     for (unsigned long n = 0; n < CTE_TABLE_SLOTS; n++, i = (i + 1) & CTE_TABLE_MASK) {
149:         if (g_table[i].addr == 0)
150:             return;
151:         if (g_table[i].addr == addr) {
152:             g_table[i].addr = 0;
153:             /* Re-insert every following non-empty slot to keep probe
154:              * chains intact (classic linear-probe deletion). */
155:             unsigned long k = (i + 1) & CTE_TABLE_MASK;
156:             while (g_table[k].addr != 0) {
157:                 cte_slot moved = g_table[k];
158:                 g_table[k].addr = 0;
159:                 cte_insert(moved.addr, moved.id, moved.size);
160:                 k = (k + 1) & CTE_TABLE_MASK;
161:             }
162:             return;
163:         }
164:     }
165: }
166: 
167: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
168: /* Event emission: one snprintf into a stack buffer, one write().      */
169: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
170: 
171: static void cte_write_all(const char *buf, size_t len)
172: {
173:     size_t off = 0;
174:     while (off < len) {
175:         ssize_t n = write(g_fd, buf + off, len - off);
176:         if (n < 0) {
177:             if (errno == EINTR)
178:                 continue;
179:             return; /* unreachable file: tracking degrades to no-op */
180:         }
181:         if (n == 0)
182:             return;
183:         off += (size_t)n;
184:     }
185: }
186: 
187: /* Caller must hold the lock. Bumps the sequence counter. */
188: static void cte_emit_locked(const char *kind, unsigned long id, unsigned long addr,
189:                             unsigned long size, unsigned long old_id, unsigned long old_addr,
190:                             unsigned long caller, const char *status)
191: {
192:     char buf[320];
193:     g_seq += 1;
194:     int n = snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%lu %lu %s %lu %lx %lu %lu %lx %lx %s\n",
195:                      (unsigned long)getpid(), g_seq, kind, id, addr, size,
196:                      old_id, old_addr, caller, status);
197:     if (n > 0)
198:         cte_write_all(buf, (size_t)n);
199: }
200: 
201: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
202: /* Lifecycle                                                           */
203: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
204: 
205: __attribute__((constructor(101)))
206: static void cte_init(void)
207: {
208:     const char *path = getenv("C_TRACE_EVENT_FILE");
209:     if (!path || !*path)
210:         return; /* passive mode: wrappers pass through, nothing recorded */
211:     g_fd = open(path, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_APPEND | O_CLOEXEC, 0600);
212: }
213: 
214: __attribute__((destructor(101)))
215: static void cte_fini(void)
216: {
217:     if (g_fd >= 0) {
218:         close(g_fd);
219:         g_fd = -1;
220:     }
221: }
222: 
223: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
224: /* Wrapped allocation functions                                        */
225: /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
226: 
227: void *__wrap_malloc(size_t size)
228: {
229:     void *ret = __real_malloc(size);
230:     if (g_busy || g_fd < 0)
231:         return ret;
232:     int saved_errno = errno;
233:     g_busy = 1;
234:     unsigned long caller = (unsigned long)__builtin_return_address(0);
235:     cte_lock();
236:     unsigned long id = ++g_ids;
237:     cte_emit_locked("malloc", id, (unsigned long)ret, size, 0, 0, caller,
238:                     ret ? "ok" : "failed");
239:     if (ret)
240:         cte_insert((unsigned long)ret, id, size);
241:     cte_unlock();
242:     g_busy = 0;
243:     errno = saved_errno;
244:     return ret;
245: }
246: 
247: void *__wrap_calloc(size_t nmemb, size_t size)
248: {
249:     void *ret = __real_calloc(nmemb, size);
250:     if (g_busy || g_fd < 0)
251:         return ret;
252:     int saved_errno = errno;
253:     g_busy = 1;
254:     unsigned long caller = (unsigned long)__builtin_return_address(0);
255:     /* The wrapped product mirrors the ABI; the real calloc validates
256:      * overflow itself (returns NULL), which we record as "failed". */
257:     int overflow = size != 0 && nmemb > SIZE_MAX / size;
258:     unsigned long total = overflow ? 0 : nmemb * size;
259:     cte_lock();
260:     unsigned long id = ++g_ids;
261:     cte_emit_locked("calloc", id, (unsigned long)ret, total, 0, 0, caller,
262:                     overflow ? "overflow" : (ret ? "ok" : "failed"));
263:     if (ret)
264:         cte_insert((unsigned long)ret, id, total);
265:     cte_unlock();
266:     g_busy = 0;
267:     errno = saved_errno;
268:     return ret;
269: }
270: 
271: void *__wrap_realloc(void *ptr, size_t size)
272: {
273:     if (g_busy || g_fd < 0)
274:         return __real_realloc(ptr, size);
275:     g_busy = 1;
276:     unsigned long caller = (unsigned long)__builtin_return_address(0);
277: 
278:     cte_lock();
279:     unsigned long old_addr = (unsigned long)ptr;
280:     cte_slot *slot = old_addr ? cte_find(old_addr) : NULL;
281:     unsigned long old_id = slot ? slot->id : 0;
282:     /* Hold the bookkeeping lock while an old address may become reusable. */
283:     void *ret = __real_realloc(ptr, size);
284:     int saved_errno = errno;
285:     unsigned long id;
286:     const char *status;
287:     if (old_addr == 0) {
288:         id = ++g_ids;
289:         status = ret ? "new" : "failed"; /* realloc(NULL, n) may fail */
290:     } else if ((unsigned long)ret == old_addr) {
291:         id = slot ? old_id : ++g_ids;
292:         status = slot ? "ok_same" : "new"; /* untracked predecessor starts observation here */
293:     } else if (ret != NULL) {
294:         id = ++g_ids;
295:         status = "ok_moved"; /* old block retired, new id for new address */
296:     } else if (size == 0) {
297:         id = old_id;
298:         status = "zero"; /* glibc: realloc(p, 0) frees p and returns NULL */
299:     } else {
300:         id = old_id;
301:         status = "failed"; /* original allocation preserved */
302:     }
303:     cte_emit_locked("realloc", id, (unsigned long)ret, size, old_id,
304:                     old_addr, caller, status);
305: 
306:     /* Table maintenance (never before emission, and state changes must
307:      * match what the real allocator actually did). */
308:     if (old_addr != 0) {
309:         if ((unsigned long)ret == old_addr) {
310:             if (slot)
311:                 slot->size = size; /* id stable, size updated */
312:             else if (ret)
313:                 cte_insert((unsigned long)ret, id, size);
314:         }
315:         else if (ret != NULL || size == 0)
316:             cte_remove(old_addr);
317:         /* status == "failed": keep the original entry */
318:     }
319:     if (ret != NULL && (old_addr == 0 || (unsigned long)ret != old_addr))
320:         cte_insert((unsigned long)ret, id, size);
321:     cte_unlock();
322:     g_busy = 0;
323:     errno = saved_errno;
324:     return ret;
325: }
326: 
327: void __wrap_free(void *ptr)
328: {
329:     if (g_busy || g_fd < 0) {
330:         __real_free(ptr);
331:         return;
332:     }
333:     g_busy = 1;
334:     unsigned long caller = (unsigned long)__builtin_return_address(0);
335:     cte_lock();
336:     unsigned long old_addr = (unsigned long)ptr;
337:     cte_slot *slot = old_addr ? cte_find(old_addr) : NULL;
338:     unsigned long id = slot ? slot->id : 0;
339:     const char *status = old_addr ? (slot ? "ok" : "unknown") : "null";
340:     unsigned long size = slot ? slot->size : 0;
341:     __real_free(ptr);
342:     int saved_errno = errno;
343:     cte_emit_locked("free", id, old_addr, size, 0, 0, caller, status);
344:     if (slot)
345:         cte_remove(old_addr);
346:     cte_unlock();
347:     g_busy = 0;
348:     errno = saved_errno;
349: }

Command line interface.

Program arguments come after `--` (e.g. `cargo run -- sample.c -- 1 2 3`) or via repeated `--arg` flags; they are handed to the traced program and never to the compiler.

Usage: c-trace-engine [OPTIONS] [SOURCE_POSITIONAL] [-- <PROGRAM_ARGS>...]

Arguments:
  [SOURCE_POSITIONAL]
          Primary C source file (positional form of --source)

  [PROGRAM_ARGS]...
          Program arguments: everything after the `--` separator (e.g. `c-trace-engine sample.c -- --flag 42`)

Options:
      --source <SOURCE>
          Primary C source file (contains main)

      --add-source <ADD_SOURCE>
          Additional C sources compiled and linked into the same binary

      --include-dir <INCLUDE_DIR>
          Include search directories (-I)

      --define <DEFINE>
          Preprocessor definitions (-D), NAME or NAME=value

      --compiler-flag <COMPILER_FLAG>
          Custom compiler flags, passed to gcc verbatim

      --linker-flag <LINKER_FLAG>
          Custom linker flags, passed to gcc verbatim

      --library-dir <LIBRARY_DIR>
          Library search directories (-L)

      --library <LIBRARY>
          Libraries to link (-l), without the leading `l`

      --object-file <OBJECT_FILE>
          Pre-built object files linked without recompilation

893:     pub async fn shutdown(mut self) {

895:         let wait = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(3), self.child.wait()).await;
896:         if matches!(wait, Ok(Err(_)) | Err(_)) {

898:                 kill_process_group(pid);
899:                 let _ = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), self.child.wait()).await;
900:             }
901:         }

904:             t.abort();

908:     /// Hard kill of the whole process group (timeout / resource limit path).
909:     /// Also kills the inferior's own process group: GDB puts the inferior in
910:     /// a separate group (job control), so killing GDB's group alone would
911:     /// leave the inferior running as an orphan.
912:     pub async fn kill(&mut self) {
913:         let cleanup_end = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(2);
914:         let mut descendants = self
915:             .child
916:             .id()
917:             .map(crate::supervisor::descendants)
918:             .unwrap_or_default();
919:         self.interrupt().await;
920:         for pid in &descendants {
921:             kill_process_group(*pid);
922:         }
923:         if let Some(pid) = self.child.id() {
924:             kill_process_group(pid);
925:         }
926:         let pid = self.shared.inferior_pid.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
927:         let inferior = (pid != 0).then_some(pid);
928:         if let Some(inferior) = inferior {
929:             if !descendants.contains(&inferior) {
930:                 descendants.push(inferior);
931:             }
932:             if self.child.id() != Some(inferior) {
933:                 kill_process_group(inferior);
934:             }
935:         }
936:         let _ = self.child.start_kill();
937:         let _ = tokio::time::timeout_at(cleanup_end.into(), self.child.wait()).await;
938:         crate::supervisor::reap_descendants(descendants, cleanup_end).await;
939:         self.inferior_pid = None;
940:         self.shared.inferior_pid.store(0, Ordering::SeqCst);
941:         self.reader_task.abort();
942:         if let Some(t) = self.pty_task.take() {
943:             t.abort();
944:         }
945:     }
946: }

948: impl Drop for GdbSession {
949:     fn drop(&mut self) {
950:         // Best effort: reader tasks are tokio tasks; abort them and ensure
951:         // neither GDB nor the inferior can outlive the session.
952:         self.reader_task.abort();
953:         if let Some(t) = self.pty_task.take() {
954:             t.abort();
955:         }
956:         if let Some(pid) = self.child.id() {
957:             kill_process_group(pid);
958:         }
959:         let pid = self.shared.inferior_pid.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
960:         let inferior = (pid != 0).then_some(pid);
961:         if let Some(inferior) = inferior {
962:             if self.child.id() != Some(inferior) {
963:                 kill_process_group(inferior);
964:             }
965:         }
966:     }
967: }

1: //! JSON trace document ingestion and input-format detection.
2: //!
3: //! The parser deliberately does not re-serialize, normalize, or "repair" the
4: //! trace: `DebugSessionTrace` is deserialized directly from the input bytes,
5: //! so what Stage 1 recorded is exactly what the [`TraceStore`](super::TraceStore)
6: //! exposes. No event renumbering, no address rewriting, no invented defaults.
7: 
8: use crate::models::DebugSessionTrace;
9: 
10: use super::error::{Result, TraceParseError};
11: 
12: /// The one schema version this engine family currently emits and accepts.
13: /// The serialized marker is the integer `2` — V2 and V2.1 share it.
14: pub(crate) const SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 2;
15: 
16: /// Human-readable summary used in error messages.
17: pub(crate) const SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION_LABEL: &str = "2 (V2 / V2.1 traces)";
18: 
19: /// Deserialize one complete JSON trace document, then gate its schema version.
20: pub(crate) fn decode_document(text: &str) -> Result<DebugSessionTrace> {
21:     let trace: DebugSessionTrace =
22:         serde_json::from_str(text).map_err(|e| TraceParseError::MalformedJson {
23:             line: e.line(),
24:             column: e.column(),
25:             message: e.to_string(),
26:         })?;
27:     validate_schema_version(&trace)?;
28:     Ok(trace)
29: }
30: 
31: /// Schema-version gate.
32: ///
33: /// A *missing* `schema_version` field is not an error: `DebugSessionTrace`
34: /// declares `#[serde(default = ...)]` returning 2, which is the engine's
35: /// documented compatibility contract for legacy V2 traces (they omit the
36: /// field and still parse). Anything other than 2 is rejected explicitly —
37: /// an incompatible version is never silently interpreted as the current one.
38: pub(crate) fn validate_schema_version(trace: &DebugSessionTrace) -> Result<()> {
39:     if trace.schema_version != SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION {
40:         return Err(TraceParseError::UnsupportedSchemaVersion {
41:             found: trace.schema_version,
42:             supported: SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION_LABEL,
43:         });
44:     }
45:     Ok(())
46: }
47: 
48: /// The input kind decided by content inspection (never by file name).
49: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
50: pub(crate) enum DetectedFormat {

# Stage 1 Evidence & Metadata Audit — c-trace-engine (V2.1)

Scope: read-only audit of the recording pipeline and trace parser... repo untouched (HEAD 486410b + TP-1..3 worktree changes unmodified). Artifacts in /tmp/opencode/audit/.

Method: code inspection (with file:line), controlled probes compiled with exact engine flags, engine runs, serde compat harness, subagent module analyses. Labels: **V** = verified in this audit; **I** = inferred from code/data; **H** = hypothesis (needs measurement); **R** = recommendation.

## A. Architecture (current)

Facts (V unless noted):
- Pipeline (src/trace.rs:1–17, 170–897): tools probe → session dir + C runtime → compile debug binary + sanitized binary → GDB/MI2 trace phase → batched addr2line → valgrind → (conditional) sanitizer → assemble.
- GDB session (src/gdb_mi.rs:9–20, 243–348): `gdb --nx --quiet --interpreter=mi2`, private pty for inferior output, one command in flight, token-matched responses, 20 s per-command timeout, session poisoned on timeout, no retries (gdb_mi.rs:40, 369–456, 435–443).
- Recorder (src/recorder.rs) journals records `configuration|checkpoint|allocation|gap|disassembly|instruction` (+`finalized` footer) (src/storage.rs:25–51); partial results preserved on timeout/crash/limit.
- Degradation ladders: sanitizer variant `address,undefined → address → undefined → none` (compiler.rs:557–578, V); diagnostics format `json → sarif-stderr → plain` (compiler.rs:10–14, V).
- Parser (src/trace_parser/*): canonical Arc<DebugSessionTrace> + shared Arc<TraceIndexes>, borrowed views, trace-local EvidenceRef, version gate `2` (json.rs:14, V).
- V2.1 removed per-instruction register capture (~90% of command time then) — register_time_us always 0 (models.rs:629–632, V).

Assessment: architecture already separates "record what happened" (Stage 1) from "interpret" (parser/views). The audit's central conclusion (R): the biggest metadata gains come from *enriching Stage 1 output* (types, liveness, identity edges), not from re-architecting.

## B. Evidence inventory (what a V2.1 trace carries today)

Per snapshot (V, probe_trace.json): step/file/line/func/call_stack(≤200), variables[] (frame-0 only; name, c_type, value, address, size_bytes, raw_bytes_hex, read/bytes status, activation_id, lexical_scope_id, identity, points_to/target, declaration_file/line), observation (stop_id, pid, origin, complete, errors, globals[], heap_event_count), heap_blocks (≤512, with raw bytes when budget allows), stdout head 64 KiB.

Per instruction event (V): event_id, position, address, source (file/line — 250/250 in probe), instruction_id → disassembly_table (197 entries), outcome; memory[] only with --memory-region (0 in probe).

Heap (V): heap_events (pid seq kind id addr size old_id old_addr caller status + addr2line file/line), heap_state, allocation_lifetimes; reuse → fresh ids.

Journals (V): 7 kinds; checkpoint records lack finalized-only fields (profiling, coverage, allocation_lifetimes, storage, source_checkpoints, instruction_count, internal_diagnostics, all top-level outcome/report fields) — identity_journal.jsonl vs identity_trace.json diff (V).

Gaps vs DWARF (see C): no type layouts, no enum values, no decl columns, no non-top-frame locals, no VLA extents pre-init, PointerTarget.variable_identity null.

## C. DWARF coverage matrix

Compiled with exact engine flags (gcc 16.2.1, `-g -O0 -fno-omit-frame-pointer`, wrap runtime) → **DWARF v5** (readelf: Version: 5) (V).

| Evidence | In DWARF | Captured by engine | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Variable location (-O0) | DW_OP_fbreg everywhere (V) | via GDB query (address) | — |
| Type *name* | yes | c_type string (V) | ok |
| struct layout (size, member offsets) | Node size 24, member @0/4/8/16 (V) | ✗ | **C** |
| union layout | Mixed size 4 (V) | ✗ | C |
| enum values | Color size 4, enumerators (V) | value only as int | C |
| bitfields | DWARF5 bit_size/data_bit_offset (V) | ✗ (bytes only) | C |
| VLA extent | DW_AT_upper_bound exprloc `fbreg:-56; deref` (V) | `int [variable length]` until initialized (V) | A/C |
| decl file/line | yes | declaration_file/line (V) | ok |
| decl column | DW_AT_decl_column present (V) | ✗ | C (minor) |
| lexical block ranges | yes (two `base` DIEs, distinct blocks) | scope_id `block:start-end:line` via GDB-Python (V) | liveness unused (B) |
| recursion/activations | n/a (runtime) | activation ids disambiguate (V) | — |
| cross-file statics | yes | `'aux.c'::counter` vs `'main.c'::counter` (V) | ok |
| non-top-frame locals | yes | ✗ frame-0 only (V: accumulate(3) snapshot shows only frame-0 vars) | C |
| source line table | yes | 100% events have file+line (V) | ok |

## D. gimli feasibility

- gimli 0.34.0 + object 0.39/0.40 present in local cargo registry; network available (V). Not integrated; nothing in Cargo.toml (V).
- Static-table extraction (layouts, enums, decl columns) is the natural gimli use; DWARF v5 support in gimli 0.34 is documented upstream but **not demonstrated in this audit** (I).
- Format limitation (V, inherent): DWARF location/extent expressions (`DW_OP_fbreg`, `DW_OP_deref`) require a frame context to evaluate — a static reader cannot resolve VLA extents or variable locations without register/CFI state. GDB is currently the evaluator (lexical_symbols, extent queries). Recommendation (R): use gimli (or keep GDB-Python) for *static* tables only; keep GDB for *dynamic* evaluation.

## E. GDB/MI opportunities

Current cadence (probe, V): 3974 commands / 68 snapshots ≈ 58/snapshot; capture 1.016 s = 42% of 2.39 s debugger phase.

Redundant work (all V by code reading):
1. `-stack-list-frames 0 199` re-issued at every capture, including non-user stops where only is_user_code is needed and the stop frame is already known (gdb_mi.rs:1300; trace.rs:1352–1361).
2. Per-variable `&`, `sizeof`, pointer-cast re-evaluated every snapshot although address/size are activation-invariant (gdb_mi.rs:1500–1520).
3. Globals: value/`&`/`sizeof`/points-to re-queried each snapshot; only type is cached (`global:{epoch}:{name}`, recorder.rs:362–381).
4. Heap blocks re-read every snapshot, no diffing, up to 512 (trace.rs:1971–2012).
5. O(n²) duplicate-name scan per capture (gdb_mi.rs:1386–1390).
6. lexical_symbols Python script re-run per checkpoint (no per-frame memoization) (gdb_mi.rs:1357–1361, 613–640).

Caching that exists (V): disassembly address cache with module_epoch invalidation (7 queries + 243 hits in probe), type cache for locals keyed by activation, one-shot scope_support probe.

Opportunities (R unless noted): scope-diff frame query; activation-keyed address/size memo; static-invariant global fields; heap read diffing (block generation counter already exists in timeline); liveness marking from block ranges (B, V data); one-time type-table dump via the same embedded-Python pattern (A); frame-N variable capture for user frames (C).

## F. Memory completeness

- Bytes evidence: per-variable raw bytes ≤ max_memory_read_bytes=4096 (V), heap block contents within a shared per-snapshot budget (V), configured --memory-region reads (V), event.memory empty without regions (V).
- Truncation is explicit (memory_truncated, bytes_status=Truncated/Unreadable) — never fabricated (V, probe observation.complete flipped false on unreadable VLA pre-init).
- Gaps: non-top-frame frame memory; no cross-snapshot diffing (bandwidth, not correctness); `/proc`-based region classification only for enrichment (memory.rs:9–47).
- Assessment: memory completeness is *bounded by configuration*, and the bounds are honest. B finding: budget currently shared such that 512 blocks × default caps can crowd out variable bytes (order of operations trace.rs:1963–2012) — inferred (I), needs measurement.

## G. Object identity

Verified scheme (V):
- Stack/frame: `activation:{id}:block:{start}-{end}:{decl_line}:{name}`; statics: `static:{scope_id}:{name}`; ambiguous: `unresolved:{activation}:...` fallback when the Python probe fails (gdb_mi.rs:1419–1427, 1459–1469).
- activation ids increment per call-path instance; recursion disambiguated (accumulate depth 3 → distinct activations, V); same names across functions distinguished (helper/alpha `value`, V).
- Heap: per-process (pid,id); serialized ids widened when fork observed; address reuse → new ids (0x705010: 1→2; 0x705740: 3→4, V).
- Pointer enrichment: lifecycle visible (null → id1 active → id1 freed → id2 at reused address, V).

Findings:
- [B, medium] `PointerTarget.variable_identity` never populated — 0 non-null across both probe traces (V). Field exists in schema; computable at enrichment by matching pointer value to a captured variable address in the same snapshot.
- [E, medium] Dangling alias after address reuse is reattributed to the *new* allocation (latest-identity preference, memory.rs:125–137): `r` (alias of freed p) resolves to id2 active:true (V). Provenance sidecar (last observed target before reuse) would disambiguate the common case (R).
- [B, medium] Pre-scope-entry locals listed with junk/zero values and read_status=valid (V: snapshot 0 lists vla/second/etc. before their decl lines); block start in scope_id + current pc ⇒ liveness computable with existing data (R).

## H. Heap instrumentation

- c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c: single unbuffered write() per event, format `pid seq kind id addr size old_id old_addr caller status` (V); linked via -Wl,--wrap (V); never touches program stdio (V).
- Rust tailing while inferior is stopped → exact prefix property (V); parse errors counted and noted (V).
- Caller resolution: one batched addr2line at end (V); source file/line on every heap event (V).
- Correlation limits (V): heap events have no per-event stop id; binding to snapshots only via heap_event_count boundaries; Valgrind correlation is (file,line)-based and deliberately conservative (valgrind.rs:375–417).
- Caps: max_heap_allocations=10_000, per-snapshot ≤512 blocks (V).

## I. Clang AST

- clang 22.1.8 parses the GNU-C probe (statement expressions, typeof, __label__, cleanup attr, __builtin_return_address) — verified after a trivial signature typo fix; gcc equally accepts (V).
- `clang -Xclang -ast-dump=json -fsyntax-only` works: 2.2 MB AST for the probe (V); preserves source-level VLA type `int[n]` (V — DWARF cannot express this as a source type); main-file filtering by loc.file required (AST includes system headers; 648 decls overall vs 19 in main) (V).
- Extraction care points (V): some nodes lack `loc` when traversing inner; callee names arrive via DeclRefExpr/UnresolvedLookupExpr children.
- Value (H until implemented): allocation call-site expression attribution, declaration-to-usage edges, source expression text; graceful degradation verified conceptually (clang optional; engine already probes tools per session) — the *engine-side* skip path is R, not yet demonstrated.

## J. Metadata-registry architecture (R, grounded in V compat)

Recommendation: one additive, per-session `type_registry` block:
- Entries keyed by a stable type key (canonical c_type string + CU/type DIE offset when available), carrying: kind, byte_size, member list (name, offset, type key, bit_size/bit_offset), enum value table, array extent expression (for VLAs), decl file/line/column.
- Variables reference entries by key (identity already carries decl_file/line to disambiguate same-name types).
- Built once per session (first checkpoint that mentions a type, or a single one-time dump after the first stop) — avoids per-checkpoint cost.
- Journal: either a new record kind (requires parser support — see L) or replay-on-finalize into the JSON only (current journal consumers unaffected).
- Parser: additive field ⇒ accepted by today's deserializer (verified); index it into TraceIndexes for O(1) lookup by views.

## K. Schema recommendations

All verified backward-compatible via the compat harness (unknown top-level field, unknown flattened-area field, new nested per-snapshot fields, legacy minimal trace — all accepted; SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION=2 unchanged):
1. Add `type_registry` (J).
2. Populate `PointerTarget.variable_identity` (existing field, no schema change).
3. Add per-variable `decl_column` (optional), `scope_live: bool` (liveness) — additive.
4. Add `provenance` sidecar on PointerTarget for dangling-before-reuse (E remedy).
5. Optionally append a `finalized`-adjacent summary record to journals (allocation_lifetimes, profiling, coverage) — needs a parser-side kind addition; version the journal format explicitly if done.

## L. Parser impact

- Today's deserializer accepts additive metadata anywhere (V, 4 cases). No version bump needed for 1–4 above (V).
- trace_parser store/views/EvidenceRef unaffected: type_registry is a new shared Arc side-table if indexed; EvidenceRef remains trace-local (ForeignTrace rejection unaffected by additive fields) (V by construction of additive JSON + existing tests).
- Journal decoder (journal.rs) validates a fixed kind set; adding a journal kind or checkpoint-record fields is a parser change — keep journal format frozen in Phase 1–2, or extend deliberately with a new kind + tests (R).

## N. Risks

1. Environment: libubsan.so.1.0.0 absent on this host ⇒ combined ASan+UBSan link fails; ladder degrades to ASan-only (V; engine note in probe trace). User remedy: install libubsan; engine behavior correct.
2. Session poisoning: one 20 s timeout kills the session permanently (no retries) — a single slow query (e.g. giant struct print) can truncate the rest of a trace (V by code; frequency unmeasured).
3. GDB-Python dependency: lexical identity + future type tables rely on embedded Python in GDB; scope_support one-shot fallback to address-based identities exists (V); GDB 18.1 verified; older GDBs untested (I).
4. Multi-threaded programs: all-stop truncates coverage after 2nd thread-created (V design); no non-stop support.
5. Caps on real programs: 256 symbol-results / 32 globals / 24 vars / 4096 bytes are demo-scale (V defaults); real projects will hit them (I) — they truncate honestly, but Stage 2 UIs should surface them.
6. gdb vs clang divergence: AST enrichment uses a different compiler's view than the one that emitted DWARF (I/H) — mitigations: feature-detect, treat AST as advisory.
7. O(n²) duplicate-name scan and per-checkpoint Python on snapshot-heavy traces (V code; impact grows with max_variables).
8. Journal is not self-sufficient (missing finalized fields) — crash-recovery consumers must not assume parity (V).

## Q. First-implement recommendation

**Phase 1 as one small, self-contained change set**, ordered by value/cost:
1. `variable_identity` population (pure enrichment at capture; no new commands).
2. Liveness marking from existing `lexical_scope_id` block ranges + current pc (no new commands; fixes misleading junk values).
3. Stale-limitation string fix (one line, recorder.rs:63–69).
Then proceed to Phase 2 (type registry) as the first *feature* — it has the highest semantic payoff and its schema addition is verified compatible.
Rationale: all three Phase-1 items are verified-feasible with existing data, require no new MI traffic, and directly serve both consumers; measurement (M) should be repeated on the probe fixture to validate the perf hypotheses before Phase 3+.

# Stage 1 Evidence & Metadata Audit — c-trace-engine (V2 / V2.1)

Read-only audit complete. The repository is untouched (HEAD `486410b`, TP-1..TP-3 changes unmodified); all experiment artifacts are in `/tmp/opencode/audit/` (report copy: `REPORT.md`).

**Evidence labels:** **V** = verified in this audit · **I** = inferred from code/data · **H** = hypothesis (needs measurement) · **R** = recommendation.
**Finding categories:** **A** = available but underutilized · **B** = existing machinery improvable · **C** = new DWARF extraction needed · **D** = optional AST enrichment · **E** = inherently uncertain/expensive · **F** = format/access limitation.

**Environment (V):** gcc 16.2.1, gdb 18.1, valgrind 3.27.1, clang 22.1.8, binutils 2.46.1; `libubsan.so.1.0.0` absent; gimli 0.34.0 + object 0.39/0.40 in local cargo registry.

---

## A. Architecture (current)

- Pipeline (src/trace.rs:1–17, 170–897): tool probes → session dir + C runtime → compile debug + sanitized binaries → GDB/MI2 trace phase → batched addr2line → Valgrind → (conditional) sanitizer → assemble. Partial results always preserved.
- GDB session (gdb_mi.rs:9–20, 243–348): `gdb --nx --quiet --interpreter=mi2`, private pty for inferior output, strictly one command in flight, token-matched responses, 20 s per-command timeout, session poisoned on timeout, no retries (gdb_mi.rs:40, 369–456, 435–443).
- Recorder journals `configuration|checkpoint|allocation|gap|disassembly|instruction` + `finalized` footer (storage.rs:25–51); raw `File` append, torn-line drop on recovery.
- Degradation ladders: sanitizer `address,undefined → address → undefined → none` (compiler.rs:557–578); diagnostics `json → sarif-stderr → plain` (compiler.rs:10–14).
- Parser: canonical `Arc<DebugSessionTrace>` + shared `Arc<TraceIndexes>`, borrowed views, trace-local `EvidenceRef` (`ForeignTrace` rejection), version gate `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2` (json.rs:14).
- V2.1 removed per-instruction register capture (~90% of command time then); `register_time_us` always 0 (models.rs:629–632).

**Assessment (R):** the architecture already separates "record what happened" from "interpret". The largest metadata gains come from *enriching Stage 1 output* (types, liveness, identity edges), not from re-architecting.

## B. Evidence inventory (what a V2.1 trace carries today)

- **Per snapshot** (V, probe_trace.json): step/file/line/func, call_stack (≤200), `variables[]` (frame-0 only; name, c_type, value, address, size_bytes, raw_bytes_hex, read/bytes status, activation_id, lexical_scope_id, identity, points_to/target, declaration_file/line), observation (stop_id, pid, origin, complete, errors, globals[], heap_event_count), heap_blocks (≤512, bytes within budget), stdout head 64 KiB.
- **Per instruction event** (V): address, source file/line (250/250), instruction_id → disassembly_table (197 entries), outcome; `memory[]` empty unless `--memory-region` (0 in probe).
- **Heap** (V): events (`pid seq kind id addr size old_id old_addr caller status` + addr2line file/line), heap_state, allocation_lifetimes; address reuse ⇒ fresh ids.
- **Journal** (V): 7 record kinds; checkpoint records lack all finalized-only fields (`allocation_lifetimes`, `profiling`, `storage`, `coverage`, `instruction_count`, `internal_diagnostics`, `source_checkpoints`, plus all top-level outcome/report fields) — verified by diffing `identity_journal.jsonl` vs `identity_trace.json`.
- **Gaps vs DWARF:** no type layouts, no enum value tables, no decl columns, no non-top-frame locals, no VLA extents pre-init, `variable_identity` never populated.

## C. DWARF coverage matrix

Fixture compiled with the exact engine flags (gcc 16.2.1, `-g -O0 -fno-omit-frame-pointer`, `-Wl,--wrap=…`) → **DWARF v5** (readelf: `Version: 5`). (V)

| Evidence | In DWARF | Captured by engine | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Variable location (−O0) | `DW_OP_fbreg` everywhere | via GDB query (address) | — |
| Type *name* | yes | `c_type` string | — |
| struct layout | `Node` size 24, members @0/4/8/16 | ✗ | **C** |
| union layout | `Mixed` size 4 | ✗ | C |
| enum values | `Color` size 4 + enumerators | value as int only | C |
| bitfields | DWARF-5 `bit_size`/`data_bit_offset` (`lo:3@0`, `hi:5`) | bytes only | C |
| VLA extent | `DW_AT_upper_bound` exprloc `fbreg:-56; deref` | `int [variable length]` until initialized | A/C |
| decl file/line | yes | `declaration_file/line` | — |
| decl column | `DW_AT_decl_column` present | ✗ | C (minor) |
| lexical block ranges | two `base` DIEs in distinct blocks | `scope_id = block:start-end:line` via GDB-Python | liveness unused (B) |
| recursion / activations | runtime property | activation ids disambiguate | — |
| cross-file statics | yes | `'aux.c'::counter` vs `'main.c'::counter` | — |
| non-top-frame locals | yes | ✗ frame-0 only (`accumulate(3)` shows only frame-0 vars) | C |
| source line table | yes | 100% events carry file+line | — |

## D. gimli feasibility

- gimli 0.34.0 + object 0.39/0.40 present in the local cargo registry; network available; not referenced by Cargo.toml. (V)
- Natural role: *static* tables (layouts, enums, decl columns, file/line). gimli 0.34's DWARF v5 support is documented upstream but **not demonstrated in this audit**. (I)
- Format limitation (V, inherent): location/extent expressions (`DW_OP_fbreg`, `DW_OP_deref`) require a frame context — a static reader cannot resolve VLA extents or variable locations without register/CFI state. GDB is the current evaluator (lexical_symbols, gdb_mi.rs:605–661).
- **R:** use gimli (or keep GDB-Python) for static tables only; keep GDB for dynamic evaluation. A demonstrated DWARF-5 probe must precede any Phase-4 commitment.

## E. GDB/MI opportunities

Cadence (probe, V): 3974 commands / 68 snapshots ≈ 58 per snapshot; capture 1.016 s = 42% of the 2.39 s debugger phase.

Redundant per-checkpoint work (V, code reading):
1. `-stack-list-frames 0 199` re-issued at every capture — including non-user stops where only `is_user_code` is needed and the stop frame is already known (gdb_mi.rs:1300; trace.rs:1352–1361).
2. Per-variable `&`, `sizeof`, pointer-cast re-evaluated every snapshot although address/size are activation-invariant (gdb_mi.rs:1500–1520).
3. Globals: value/`&`/`sizeof`/points-to re-queried each snapshot; only type is cached (`global:{epoch}:{name}`, recorder.rs:362–381).
4. Heap blocks re-read every snapshot with no diffing, up to 512 (trace.rs:1971–2012).
5. O(n²) duplicate-name scan per capture (gdb_mi.rs:1386–1390).
6. `lexical_symbols` Python script re-run per checkpoint (no per-frame memoization) (gdb_mi.rs:1357–1361, 613–640).

Caching that exists (V): disassembly address cache with `module_epoch` invalidation (7 queries + 243 hits in probe); local type cache keyed by activation; one-shot `scope_support` probe.

**Opportunities (R):** scope-diff frame query; activation-keyed address/size memoization; static-invariant global fields; heap read diffing (timeline already knows block generations); liveness marking from block ranges; one-time type-table dump via the same embedded-Python pattern; frame-N variable capture for user frames.

## F. Memory completeness

- Byte evidence: per-variable raw bytes ≤ 4096; heap contents within a shared 1 MiB snapshot budget; configured `--memory-region` reads; `InstructionEvent.memory` empty without regions. (V)
- Truncation is explicit (`memory_truncated`, `bytes_status` = Truncated/Unreadable) and never fabricated — verified: the pre-init VLA read failure correctly flipped `observation.complete = false`. (V)
- Gaps: no non-top-frame frame memory; no cross-snapshot diffing (bandwidth, not correctness); `/proc` classification only for enrichment (memory.rs:9–47).
- **I:** shared-budget ordering (trace.rs:1963–2012) can let 512 heap blocks crowd out variable bytes on heap-heavy traces — needs measurement.

## G. Object identity

Verified scheme (V):
- Frame locals: `activation:{id}:block:{start}-{end}:{decl_line}:{name}`; statics: `static:{scope_id}:{name}`; ambiguous fallback `unresolved:{activation}:…` when the Python probe fails (gdb_mi.rs:1419–1427, 1459–1469).
- Activation ids increment per call-path instance; recursion disambiguated (`accumulate(3)` → distinct activations); same names across functions distinguished.
- Heap: per-process `(pid, id)`; ids widened on fork; address reuse ⇒ fresh ids (0x705010: 1→2; 0x705740: 3→4).
- Pointer enrichment shows the full lifecycle: null → id1 active → id1 freed → id2 at the reused address.

Findings:
- **[B, medium]** `PointerTarget.variable_identity` never populated — 0 non-null occurrences across both probe traces (V). Computable at enrichment by matching the pointer value to a captured variable address in the same snapshot.
- **[E, medium]** Dangling alias after address reuse is reattributed to the *new* allocation (latest-identity preference, memory.rs:125–137): `r` (alias of freed `p`) resolved to id2 `active:true` (V). A provenance sidecar ("last observed target before reuse") would disambiguate the common case. (R)
- **[B, medium]** Pre-scope-entry locals are listed with junk/zero values and `read_status = valid` (V: snapshot 0 lists `vla`, `second`, … before their decl lines). Block start inside `lexical_scope_id` + current pc make liveness computable from data already collected. (R)

## H. Heap instrumentation

- `c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c`: one unbuffered `write()` per event; format `pid seq kind id addr size old_id old_addr caller status`; linked via `-Wl,--wrap=…`; never touches program stdio. (V)
- Rust tailing while the inferior is stopped ⇒ exact event prefix at every read; parse errors counted and noted. (V)
- One batched `addr2line` at end; every heap event carries resolved file/line. (V)
- Correlation limits (V): no per-event stop id; snapshot binding only via `heap_event_count` boundaries; Valgrind correlation is (file, line)-based and deliberately conservative (valgrind.rs:375–417).
- Caps: `max_heap_allocations = 10_000`; ≤512 blocks per snapshot. (V)

2. Liveness marking from existing `lexical_scope_id` block ranges + current pc (no new commands; removes misleading junk values).
3. Fix the stale limitation string (one line, recorder.rs:63–69).

Then proceed to **Phase 2 (type registry)** as the first feature — highest semantic payoff, and its schema addition is verified compatible. Rationale: all three Phase-1 items are verified-feasible with data already collected, add no MI traffic, and serve both consumers; repeat the M measurements on the probe fixture to validate the perf hypotheses before committing to Phase 3+.

12: # Find Skills
13: 
14: This skill helps you discover and install skills from the open agent skills ecosystem.
15: 
16: ## When to Use This Skill
17: 
18: Use this skill when the user:
19: 
20: - Asks "how do I do X" where X might be a common task with an existing skill
21: - Says "find a skill for X" or "is there a skill for X"
22: - Asks "can you do X" where X is a specialized capability
23: - Expresses interest in extending agent capabilities
24: - Wants to search for tools, templates, or workflows
25: - Mentions they wish they had help with a specific domain (design, testing, deployment, etc.)
26: 
27: ## What is the Skills CLI?
28: 
29: The Skills CLI (`npx skills`) is the package manager for the open agent skills ecosystem. Skills are modular packages that extend agent capabilities with specialized knowledge, workflows, and tools.
30: 
31: **Key commands:**
32: 
33: - `npx skills find [query] [--owner <owner>]` - Search for skills interactively or by keyword, optionally scoped to a GitHub owner
34: - `npx skills add <package>` - Install a skill from GitHub or other sources
35: - `npx skills update` - Update all installed skills
36: 
37: **Browse skills at:** https://skills.sh/
38: 
39: ## How to Help Users Find Skills
40: 
41: ### Step 1: Understand What They Need
42: 
43: When a user asks for help with something, identify:
44: 
45: 1. The domain (e.g., React, testing, design, deployment)
46: 2. The specific task (e.g., writing tests, creating animations, reviewing PRs)
47: 3. Whether this is a common enough task that a skill likely exists
48: 
49: ### Step 2: Check the Leaderboard First
50: 
51: Before running a CLI search, check the [skills.sh leaderboard](https://skills.sh/) to see if a well-known skill already exists for the domain. The leaderboard ranks skills by total installs, surfacing the most popular and battle-tested options.
52: 
53: For example, top skills for web development include:
54: - `vercel-labs/agent-skills` — React, Next.js, web design (100K+ installs each)
55: - `anthropics/skills` — Frontend design, document processing (100K+ installs)
56: 
57: ### Step 3: Search for Skills
58: 
59: If the leaderboard doesn't cover the user's need, run the find command:
60: 
61: ```bash
62: npx skills find [query] [--owner <owner>]
63: ```
64: 
65: For example:
66: 
67: - User asks "how do I make my React app faster?" → `npx skills find react performance`
68: - User asks "can you help me with PR reviews?" → `npx skills find pr review`
69: - User asks "I need to create a changelog" → `npx skills find changelog`
70: 
71: ### Step 4: Verify Quality Before Recommending
72: 
73: **Do not recommend a skill based solely on search results.** Always verify:
74: 
75: 1. **Install count** — Prefer skills with 1K+ installs. Be cautious with anything under 100.
76: 2. **Source reputation** — Official sources (`vercel-labs`, `anthropics`, `microsoft`) are more trustworthy than unknown authors.
77: 3. **GitHub stars** — Check the source repository. A skill from a repo with <100 stars should be treated with skepticism.
78: 
79: ### Step 5: Present Options to the User
80: 
81: When you find relevant skills, present them to the user with:
82: 
83: 1. The skill name and what it does
84: 2. The install count and source
85: 3. The install command they can run
86: 4. A link to learn more at skills.sh
87: 
88: Example response:
89: 
90: ```
91: I found a skill that might help! The "react-best-practices" skill provides
92: React and Next.js performance optimization guidelines from Vercel Engineering.
93: (185K installs)
94: 
95: To install it:
96: npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills@react-best-practices
97: 
98: Learn more: https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-skills/react-best-practices
99: ```
100: 
101: ### Step 6: Offer to Install
102: 
103: If the user wants to proceed, you can install the skill for them:
104: 
105: ```bash
106: npx skills add <owner/repo@skill> -g -y
107: ```
108: 
109: The `-g` flag installs globally (user-level) and `-y` skips confirmation prompts.
110: 
111: ## Common Skill Categories
112: 
113: When searching, consider these common categories:
114: 
115: | Category        | Example Queries                          |
116: | --------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
117: | Web Development | react, nextjs, typescript, css, tailwind |
118: | Testing         | testing, jest, playwright, e2e           |
119: | DevOps          | deploy, docker, kubernetes, ci-cd        |
120: | Documentation   | docs, readme, changelog, api-docs        |
121: | Code Quality    | review, lint, refactor, best-practices   |
122: | Design          | ui, ux, design-system, accessibility     |
123: | Productivity    | workflow, automation, git                |
124: 
125: ## Tips for Effective Searches
126: 
127: 1. **Use specific keywords**: "react testing" is better than just "testing"
128: 2. **Try alternative terms**: If "deploy" doesn't work, try "deployment" or "ci-cd"
129: 3. **Check popular sources**: Many skills come from `vercel-labs/agent-skills` or `ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills`
130: 
131: ## When No Skills Are Found
132:

137: 3. Suggest the user could create their own skill with `npx skills init`

147: ```

# 5. Improvement A — Pointer-to-variable identity

## The problem

Consider:

```c
int main(void) {
    int x = 10;
    int *p = &x;

    *p = 20;
}
```

Stage 1 can observe:

- The address of `x`.
- The value stored in `p`.
- The identity of `x`.
- The current stack activation.

However, the current `PointerTarget.variable_identity` remains empty.

We want the trace to preserve the relationship between `p` and `x` when supported by actual observations.

## Expected behavior

If the current checkpoint provides:

```text
Variable x:
    address = 0x1000
    identity = activation:1:...:x

Variable p:
    value = 0x1000
```

And the target is unambiguously identified:

```text
PointerTarget.variable_identity =
    activation:1:...:x
```

These addresses and identities are illustrative.

Use the actual Stage 1 data model.

## Implementation requirements

Extend the existing pointer enrichment path.

Use:

- Recorded variable addresses.
- Existing variable identities.
- Available stack-frame activation information.
- Existing lexical-scope information.
- Available global/static variable observations.
- The current checkpoint's recorded pointer values.

### Correctness rules

**Rule 1 — Identity must come from existing evidence.**

Do not invent new variable identities based solely on names or addresses.

Reuse the identity assigned by the existing recorder.

**Rule 2 — Match the current execution context.**

Do not associate a pointer with a local variable from an unrelated invocation or earlier execution context.

**Rule 3 — Handle ambiguity honestly.**

If multiple visible objects could match the same address, do not arbitrarily choose one.

Leave the identity unresolved unless existing evidence establishes a unique target.

**Rule 4 — Respect object boundaries.**

A pointer to the beginning of a variable may be resolvable.

A pointer into the middle of an array, structure, or other aggregate must not automatically be assigned to an arbitrary variable without sufficient extent and identity evidence.

Preserve any existing pointer offset information.

**Rule 5 — Preserve heap identity.**

If a pointer targets a tracked heap allocation, preserve its allocation identity and existing heap metadata.

Do not replace heap identity with an unrelated variable identity.

**Rule 6 — Null and unavailable pointers remain unresolved.**

Do not manufacture target identities for null pointers, unreadable pointer values, or addresses that cannot be matched.

**Rule 7 — No stale matches.**

If an address was reused after a stack activation ended, do not assign an old activation's variable identity to the new context.

## Performance requirements

Avoid an expensive nested scan for every pointer-variable pair.

If useful, build a lightweight temporary address-to-observed-variable lookup for each checkpoint.

Prefer linear or near-linear processing relative to the variables and pointers in the checkpoint.

Do not create a persistent global cache of temporary stack addresses without proper lifetime semantics.

Do not introduce additional GDB commands.

---

# 6. Improvement B — Variable scope liveness

## The problem

Consider:

```c
int main(void) {
    int first = 10;

    {
        int second = 20;
    }

    return 0;
}
```

The debugger may know that `second` exists as a declaration even before execution reaches its lexical block.

However, that does not mean `second` is currently an active variable with a meaningful value.

The audit found that Stage 1 sometimes records variables before their scope becomes active, displaying junk or zero values as valid observations.

This can mislead beginners.

## Required investigation

Inspect how `lexical_scope_id` is generated.

Determine whether the existing debugger information distinguishes:

- Current active lexical block.
- Enclosing lexical blocks.
- Variables declared in those blocks.
- Variables belonging to inactive blocks.
- Function parameters.
- Function-scope locals.
- Globals and static variables.

Determine whether block ranges are represented using instruction addresses, source locations, or another scheme.

Do not assume that a string containing a starting line is sufficient to establish runtime liveness.

## Important conceptual distinction

These properties are different:

**Lexical scope:** Where a name is visible according to C's scoping rules.

**Storage lifetime:** When an object exists during execution.

**Initialization state:** Whether the program has established a meaningful value.

**Memory readability:** Whether GDB successfully read bytes from an address.

Do not merge all four into one status.

In particular:

**A successful memory read does not prove that a variable is initialized.**

And observing a variable's declaration does not prove that its scope is currently active.

## Required behavior

Where the existing evidence is sufficient, expose whether a variable's lexical scope is currently active.

Prefer a representation that distinguishes:

- Active.
- Inactive.
- Unknown or unresolved.

A nullable boolean or a small typed status may be suitable.

Choose based on the existing schema and project conventions.

### Critical rules

1. Do not mark a variable inactive solely because the current source line is numerically earlier than its declaration line.
2. Do not infer initialization solely from scope membership.
3. Do not assume source line order exactly matches machine execution order.
4. Do not assume all variables are active throughout a function.
5. Do not confuse stack-frame depth with activation identity.
6. Do not discard legitimately observed raw bytes simply because the source-level variable is inactive.
7. Do not report logically valid variable values when scope evidence establishes that the declaration is inactive.
8. If scope evaluation is inconclusive, represent it as unknown.
9. Preserve actual read-success or read-failure information separately.

### Scope implementation

Prefer reusing existing lexical-scope metadata and execution-location information.

If the current GDB-Python lexical-symbol probe already exposes sufficient information, use it.

Keep scope interpretation contained within the appropriate existing recording or enrichment component.

Do not introduce unrelated scope-analysis logic throughout the engine.

### Compatibility

If an additive field is necessary, use an optional Serde representation with suitable defaults.

Existing V2.1 traces must remain readable.

Do not change the meaning of existing fields.

Do not bump the schema version solely to add a backward-compatible optional field.

# 10. Required test scenarios

Add focused regression tests.

## A. Simple pointer relationships

```c
int x = 10;
int *p = &x;
```

Verify that the pointer can reference the correct recorded variable identity when the observation is available.

## B. Pointer reassignment

```c
int x = 10;
int y = 20;

int *p = &x;
p = &y;
```

Verify identities correspond to the actual recorded pointer targets.

Do not retain stale associations.

## C. Pointer aliases

```c
int x = 10;

int *p = &x;
int *q = p;
```

Verify both pointers can resolve to the same variable identity when the recorded evidence supports it.

## D. Null pointers

```c
int *p = 0;
```

Verify that no variable identity is invented.

## E. Nested lexical scopes

```c
int main(void) {
    int a = 10;

    {
        int b = 20;
    }

    return 0;
}
```

Verify that the scope status for `b` reflects actual lexical-scope evidence rather than an unconditional valid state.

## F. Variable shadowing

```c
int main(void) {
    int x = 10;

    {
        int x = 20;
        int *p = &x;
    }

    return 0;
}
```

Verify that identities distinguish the two declarations and that scope-sensitive pointer resolution does not select the wrong `x`.

## G. Recursive calls

Use a small recursive function with local variables.

Verify distinct activation identities and no cross-activation identity confusion.

## H. Stack address reuse

Call the same function repeatedly.

Verify that pointer identity resolution does not confuse separate function activations merely because they use the same stack address.

## I. Array interior pointers

```c
int a[3] = {10, 20, 30};
int *p = &a[1];
```

Verify conservative handling when the current evidence cannot uniquely identify an interior target.

Do not fabricate element identities.

## J. Heap pointers

```c
int *p = malloc(sizeof(int));
```

Verify that existing allocation identities remain intact.

Do not incorrectly assign a local-variable identity to heap memory.

## K. Unavailable evidence

Test cases where:

- Variable addresses are absent.
- Pointer values are unreadable.
- Lexical scope information is missing.
- Identity enrichment fails.
- Several candidate objects overlap.

Verify explicit unresolved behavior.

## L. Existing trace fixtures

Run all relevant V2.1 fixtures.

Verify that existing observations remain intact except for intentional correctness improvements.

Cases where line-order misleads: loops (jump back to earlier line — but decl_line is a single point; a var can't be declared twice), goto into middle of loop skipping declarations?? C: jumping into a block past a declaration with initializer is illegal-ish (GCC allows with warning for VLAs; labels + goto can skip initializers! `goto` over `int x = 5;` → x exists but uninitialized — value is junk, and marking it "inactive" would be WRONG per C semantics: the variable IS in scope, just uninitialized). Also: multiple functions same file (decl_line across functions — mitigated by matching function name & file), switch-case jumps into blocks (Duff's device!), etc. The spec explicitly warns about these ("Do not assume source line order exactly matches machine execution order").

/// Lexical-scope activity for one recorded variable, evaluated at the
/// checkpoint where it was captured.
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ScopeStatus {
    /// The variable's defining lexical block range contains the frame's
    /// program counter at capture time.
    Active,
    /// Recorded lexical-scope evidence places the frame's program counter
    /// outside the variable's defining lexical block.
    Inactive,
    /// Lexical-scope evidence was unavailable or inconclusive.
    Unknown,
}
```

9: pub fn storage_region(pid: u32, addr: u64) -> Option<&'static str> {
10:     let maps = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{pid}/maps")).ok()?;
11:     for line in maps.lines() {
12:         let fields: Vec<_> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
13:         let (start, end) = fields.first()?.split_once('-')?;
14:         let start = u64::from_str_radix(start, 16).ok()?;
15:         let end = u64::from_str_radix(end, 16).ok()?;
16:         if addr >= start && addr < end {
17:             return match fields.get(5).copied() {
18:                 Some("[stack]") => Some("stack"),
19:                 Some(path) if path.starts_with('/') => Some("static"),
20:                 _ => None,
21:             };
22:         }
23:     }
24:     None
25: }

27: fn mapping_kind(pid: u32, addr: u64) -> Option<&'static str> {
28:     let maps = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{pid}/maps")).ok()?;
29:     let mut observed = false;
30:     for line in maps.lines() {
31:         let fields: Vec<_> = line.split_whitespace().collect();

35:         observed = true;

40:                 Some("stack")
41:             } else {
42:                 None
43:             };
44:         }
45:     }
46:     observed.then_some("unmapped")
47: }

49: /// ELF64 little-endian executable load bias using a real PT_LOAD mapping.
50: /// Unsupported ELF formats return None, never a guessed relocation.
51: pub fn executable_bias(binary: &std::path::Path, pid: u32) -> Option<u64> {
52:     let elf = std::fs::read(binary).ok()?;
53:     if elf.get(..6)? != b"\x7fELF\x02\x01" {
54:         return None;
55:     }
56:     let u64_at = |offset: usize| -> Option<u64> {
57:         Some(u64::from_le_bytes(
58:             elf.get(offset..offset + 8)?.try_into().ok()?,
59:         ))
60:     };
61:     let u16_at = |offset: usize| -> Option<u16> {
62:         Some(u16::from_le_bytes(
63:             elf.get(offset..offset + 2)?.try_into().ok()?,
64:         ))
65:     };
66:     if u16_at(16)? == 2 {
67:         return Some(0);
68:     } // ET_EXEC
69:     if u16_at(16)? != 3 {
70:         return None;
71:     } // ET_DYN (PIE)
72:     let phoff = usize::try_from(u64_at(32)?).ok()?;
73:     let entsize = u16_at(54)? as usize;
74:     let count = u16_at(56)? as usize;
75:     let path = std::fs::canonicalize(binary).ok()?.display().to_string();
76:     let maps = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{pid}/maps")).ok()?;
77:     for line in maps.lines() {
78:         let fields: Vec<_> = line.split_whitespace().collect();
79:         if fields.len() < 6 || fields[5] != path {
80:             continue;
81:         }
82:         let start = u64::from_str_radix(fields[0].split('-').next()?, 16).ok()?;
83:         let offset = u64::from_str_radix(fields[2], 16).ok()?;
84:         for i in 0..count {
85:             let p = phoff.checked_add(i.checked_mul(entsize)?)?;
86:             let kind = u32::from_le_bytes(elf.get(p..p + 4)?.try_into().ok()?);
87:             if kind != 1 {
88:                 continue;
89:             }
90:             let file_offset = u64_at(p + 8)?;
91:             let vaddr = u64_at(p + 16)?;
92:             if offset == file_offset & !4095 {
93:                 return start.checked_sub(vaddr & !4095);
94:             }
95:         }
96:     }
97:     None
98: }

100: pub fn enrich(
101:     vars: &mut [VariableInfo],
102:     globals: &[VariableInfo],
103:     timeline: &HeapTimeline,
104:     pid: Option<u32>,
105: ) {
106:     let known: Vec<_> = vars
107:         .iter()
108:         .chain(globals)
109:         .filter_map(|v| {
110:             Some((
111:                 address(v.address.as_deref()?)?,
112:                 v.size_bytes?,
113:                 v.identity.clone(),
114:                 v.scope.clone(),
115:             ))
116:         })
117:         .collect();
118:     for var in vars {
119:         let Some(target) = var.points_to.as_deref().and_then(address) else {
120:             continue;
121:         };
122:         let mut info = PointerTarget::default();
123:         if target == 0 {
124:             info.kind = "null".into();
125:         } else if let Some(b) = timeline.blocks().iter().rev().find(|b| {
126:             Some(b.pid) == pid
127:                 && target >= b.addr
128:                 && target
129:                     .checked_sub(b.addr)
130:                     .is_some_and(|off| off < b.size || (off == 0 && b.size == 0))
131:         }) {
132:             info.kind = "heap".into();
133:             info.allocation_id = Some(timeline.global_id(b.pid, b.allocation_id));
134:             info.base_address = Some(format!("0x{:x}", b.addr));
135:             info.offset_bytes = Some(target - b.addr);
136:             info.active = Some(!b.freed);
137:             info.within_extent = Some(target - b.addr < b.size);
138:         } else if let Some((base, _, identity, scope)) = known
139:             .iter()
140:             .find(|(base, size, _, _)| target >= *base && target - base < *size)
141:         {
142:             info.kind = match scope.as_deref() {
143:                 Some("global") => "global",
144:                 Some("static") => "static",
145:                 Some("stack") => "stack",
146:                 _ => "unknown",
147:             }
148:             .into();
149:             info.base_address = Some(format!("0x{base:x}"));
150:             info.offset_bytes = Some(target - base);
151:             info.variable_identity = identity.clone();
152:         } else if let Some(kind) = pid.and_then(|pid| mapping_kind(pid, target)) {
153:             info.kind = kind.into();
154:         }
155:         var.target = Some(info);
156:     }
157: }

/* Pointer demonstration: own address vs. pointed-to address, writes through
 * pointers, address-of locals, pointer arithmetic on heap memory. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(void) {
    int value = 42;
    int *p = &value;
    int *heap = malloc(4 * sizeof(int));
    if (heap == 0) {
        return 1;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        heap[i] = i * 10;
    }
    int *third = heap + 2;
    *p = *third + 2; /* value becomes 22 */
    printf("value=%d heap[3]=%d\n", value, heap[3]);
    free(heap);
    return 0;
}
#include <stdlib.h>
int main(void) {
    char *a = malloc(32);
    free(a);
    char *b = malloc(32);
    if (!b) return 1;
    b[0] = 1;
    free(b);
    return 0;
}
static int recurse(int value) {
    if (value == 0) return 1;
    int result = recurse(value - 1);
    return result + value;
}
int main(void) {
    int value = recurse(3);
    return value == 7 ? 0 : 1;
}

#include <stdlib.h>

**Now the models edit**:

```rust
/// Lexical-scope activity of one recorded variable, evaluated at the stop
/// where it was captured. This describes **lexical scope activity only**:
/// it never implies that a declaration's initializer has executed, that
/// storage exists, or that a value is meaningful. Readability remains in
/// `bytes_status`; value validity remains in `read_status`.
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ScopeStatus {
    /// Recorded lexical-scope evidence places the frame's program counter
    /// inside the variable's defining block address range.
    Active,
    /// Recorded lexical-scope evidence places the frame's program counter
    /// outside that range.
    Inactive,
    /// Scope evidence was missing or inconclusive.
    Unknown,
}
```

```rust
/// Lexical-scope activity for one captured variable, from already-recorded
/// evidence only: the variable's defining block range (`block:<start>-<end>:<line>`,
/// instruction addresses emitted by the GDB-Python lexical probe) and the
/// captured frame-0 program counter.
///
/// `Active`/`Inactive` are claims about **lexical scope activity**, never
/// about initialization: at `-O0` a function-body local's defining block
/// spans its whole activation, so an initializer that has not executed yet
/// does not make the scope inactive. Inconclusive evidence (missing probe
/// output, unparsable ids, no frame address) is `Unknown`.
pub(crate) fn lexical_scope_status(
    lexical_scope_id: Option<&str>,
    frame_address: Option<&str>,
) -> crate::models::ScopeStatus {
    use crate::models::ScopeStatus;
    let Some(id) = lexical_scope_id else {
        return ScopeStatus::Unknown;
    };
    let Some(rest) = id.strip_prefix("block:") else {
        return ScopeStatus::Unknown;
    };
    let Some((range, _line)) = rest.split_once(':') else {
        return ScopeStatus::Unknown;
    };
    let Some((start, end)) = range.split_once('-') else {
        return ScopeStatus::Unknown;
    };
    let (Ok(start), Ok(end)) = (
        u64::from_str_radix(start, 16),
        u64::from_str_radix(end, 16),
    ) else {
        return ScopeStatus::Unknown;
    };
    let Some(pc) = frame_address.and_then(crate::memory::address) else {
        return ScopeStatus::Unknown;
    };
    if start <= pc && pc < end {
        ScopeStatus::Active
    } else {
        ScopeStatus::Inactive
    }
}
```

pub fn enrich(
    vars: &mut [VariableInfo],
    globals: &[VariableInfo],
    timeline: &HeapTimeline,
    pid: Option<u32>,
) {
    // Address -> candidate lookup for this checkpoint. Candidates keep the
    // recorder's identities; no identities are invented here. Indices refer
    // to `vars` (0..vars.len()) then `globals`.
    enum Source { Var(usize), Global(usize) }
    let mut known: Vec<(u64, u64, Source)> = Vec::new();
    for (i, v) in vars.iter().enumerate() {
        if let (Some(base), Some(size)) = (v.address.as_deref().and_then(address), v.size_bytes) {
            known.push((base, size, Source::Var(i)));
        }
    }
    for (j, g) in globals.iter().enumerate() {
        if let (Some(base), Some(size)) = (g.address.as_deref().and_then(address), g.size_bytes) {
            known.push((base, size, Source::Global(j)));
        }
    }
    let scope_of = |src: &Source| -> Option<&str> {
        match src {
            Source::Var(i) => vars[*i].scope.as_deref(),
            Source::Global(j) => globals[*j].scope.as_deref(),
        }
    };
    let identity_of = |src: &Source| -> Option<&str> {
        match src {
            Source::Var(i) => vars[*i].identity.as_deref(),
            Source::Global(j) => globals[*j].identity.as_deref(),
        }
    };
    for i in 0..vars.len() {
        let Some(target) = vars[i].points_to.as_deref().and_then(address) else { continue; };
        let mut info = PointerTarget::default();
        if target == 0 {
            info.kind = "null".into();
        } else if let Some(b) = timeline... { ... unchanged ... }
        else {
            // containment candidates in the same order the previous
            // first-match scan used (vars before globals)
            let matches: Vec<&(u64,u64,Source)> = known.iter().filter(|(base, size, _)| target >= *base && target - *base < *size).collect();
            if let Some(first) = matches.first() {
                info.kind = match scope_of(&first.2) { ... }.into();
                info.base_address = Some(format!("0x{:x}", first.0));
                info.offset_bytes = Some(target - first.0);
                // Identity only when exactly one object contains the target
                // and the recorder assigned a definite identity to it.
                if matches.len() == 1 {

                    }

            } else if let Some(kind) = pid.and_then(|pid| mapping_kind(pid, target)) {
                info.kind = kind.into();
            }
        }
        vars[i].target = Some(info);
    }
}

/* V2.2 Phase 1 scope-liveness scenarios: nested lexical scopes (E),
 * shadowing (F), recursion with distinct activations (G), and stack
 * address reuse across sequential activations (H). */

static int helper(int depth, int **captured) {

    if (depth == 0) {
        *captured = &local;
        return local;
    }
    return helper(depth - 1, captured);
}

        r = helper(2, &self);
    }
    return x + r;
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn valgrind_path_override_allows_failure_injection() {
    let Some(_permit) = tools().await else {
        return;
    };
    let mut c = config("pointer_demo.c");
    c.valgrind_path = Some("/nonexistent/cannot-be-valgrind".into());
    let t = trace_program(c).await.unwrap();
    // GDB execution is unaffected; Valgrind discovery fails and is skipped
    // with an explanatory note (never silently).
    assert_eq!(t.execution_status, ExecutionStatus::Completed);
    assert_eq!(t.stage_results.valgrind.status, Some(StageStatus::Skipped));
    assert!(t.valgrind_report.is_none());
    assert!(t
        .analysis_notes
        .iter()
        .any(|n| n.contains("valgrind not found")));
}
